In a new paper published in The Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
, researchers from IBM Quantum® and Lockheed Martin demonstrate how a quantum computer can help accurately model the electronic structure of certain molecules. These so-called, “open-shell” molecules contain one or more unpaired electrons, making them difficult to simulate with classical methods alone.
The new research marks the first application of the sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) technique to open-shell systems — an important milestone for quantum chemistry and its applications in aerospace, sensing, and materials design. IBM® researchers believe that SQD is a prime candidate for near-term demonstrations of quantum advantage, as it allows researchers to combine the best of high-performance quantum computers and high-performance classical computers in tackling interesting simulation problems.
Quantum computing for chemistry: Why now?
Quantum chemistry has long stood out as one of the most promising applications for quantum computing. Many chemical systems — particularly those involving strong electron correlation, e.g., transition metals, radical species, transition states, or excited states — are exceptionally hard to simulate using classical high-performance computing.
The computational cost of exactly modeling these systems with classical computers grows exponentially with the number of interacting electrons, making exact solutions practically inaccessible for even relatively small molecules. While there are some classical approximation methods that can simulate chemical systems with strong electronic correlation, these methods are computationally expensive.
This is where quantum computers could come in. Quantum chemistry simulations run on quantum computers can accurately compute the electronic structure and energies of these systems as an alternative to classical methods. As quantum computers progress toward fault-tolerance, it is possible that they will be able to simulate strongly correlated systems more accurately and at much larger scales than any classical approximation method.
One especially important quantity in computational chemistry is the energy difference between the electronic states of a molecule, such as the gap between a singlet and a triplet state — more on those later. These electronic transitions play a central role in everything from chemical reactivity and photochemistry to material properties and molecular sensing.
Accurately computing transition energies enables scientists to:
Predict reactivity and mechanisms in catalytic and combustion reactions
Design molecules with tailored optical or electronic properties, such as fluorescent probes or solar absorbers
Model excited-state behavior in materials used for sensing, display technologies, or aerospace applications
Benchmark and validate experiments in cases where measurements are difficult, dangerous, or expensive
But accurate calculation of transition energies is also extremely challenging. As molecules become more complex, the number of possible interactions between electrons (i.e., the electron correlation) grows exponentially. Capturing these interactions accurately, especially when electrons are strongly correlated or unpaired (as in radical species), pushes classical computing methods to their limits.
Things become even
more
challenging when we’re dealing with open-shell molecules, i.e., molecules that have unpaired electrons in their electronic configuration. Closed-shell molecules tend to have relatively simple, stable wavefunctions because all electrons are paired in orbitals. Open-shell systems are more complex. They can exhibit magnetic properties, high reactivity, and complex “multi-reference” electronic structures where we must rely on multiple wave functions to capture the full complexity. These characteristics make open-shell systems incredibly important in fields like combustion chemistry, catalysis, and atmospheric science — but also make them difficult to model accurately.
Open-shell species include radicals, transition metal complexes, and intermediate states in chemical reactions. Because their unpaired electrons create a rich but difficult-to-capture correlation structure, traditional classical methods often struggle with them — either oversimplifying the physics or requiring extensive computational resources.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News（HN）评论和讨论对个人生活和职业发展的影响

不同观点：
• Esperent分享了自己如何将技术技能应用于非技术性业务（面包店）并取得成功。他的经历表明，技术人员在非技术性业务中可以通过技能互补创造巨大价值，尽管过程中面临许多挑战。
• Joshstrange表示HN对他的生活产生了深远影响，尽管无法具体指出哪一篇帖子。他提到HN为他提供了技术讨论和新闻的平台，帮助他在工作和个人成长中获得优势。
• Rahimnathwani通过HN推荐的书籍《Teach your child to read in 100 easy lessons》成功教会儿子的阅读，这对他儿子的语言和认知发展产生了积极影响。
• Nothercastle提到一篇关于核能和太阳能成本比较的博客文章改变了他对能源问题的看法，使他意识到主流媒体未充分讨论的能源经济问题。
• Ggm认为HN评论与帖子的比例可能导致负面影响，因此他调整了自己的发帖习惯，减少无意义的争论，更多地分享有价值的内容，这让他变得更加积极。
• Caro_kann提到一篇关于AI工具UI/UX的帖子激发了他创建新事物的欲望，并改变了他对AI工具设计的看法。
• Brudgers欣赏HN内容的多样性，认为它提供了许多未听闻或新角度的信息，比主流媒体的八卦新闻更有价值。
• Interestoo分享了身边有人在HN的“谁想被雇佣”帖子中成功找到工作的故事，这改变了他对该板块的怀疑态度。
• Efortis提到一篇关于SketchLab的帖子对他产生了深远影响，尽管原因过于私人不便公开。
• D--b提到一篇鼓励开始项目的帖子帮助他减轻了对项目规模的恐惧，使他成功推出产品并完成剧本写作。
• Bitwize引用了一篇让他感到职业生涯被浪费的帖子，该帖讨论了当前计算的重要性和AI对编程的未来影响，使他感到如果不年轻就可能被淘汰。
• __Rito__详细列举了HN对他生活的多方面积极影响，包括书籍推荐、MOOC课程学习、技术知识的提升以及对右翼观点的理性认识。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户通过HN获得了不同的启发和改变，包括职业发展、个人技能提升、家庭教育和世界观的拓展。
• HN的影响力不仅限于技术和创业话题，还包括书籍、教育、社会问题等多方面，使用户在广泛的领域中受益。
• 一些用户提到HN的高质量讨论和直接来源链接帮助他们更深入地理解问题，并提升了自己的判断力。
• 争议焦点在于HN上某些评论可能带来的负面情绪或自我怀疑，如bitwize感受到的职业焦虑，但总体上积极影响更为显著。

data.title: Infrared contact lenses allow people to see in the dark, eyes closed
data.author: joak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种由中国科技大学研究人员开发的 infrared（红外线）隐形眼镜，它可以在无需电源的情况下将红外光转换为可见光，使佩戴者在黑暗中甚至闭眼时也能看到红外线。这种技术利用纳米颗粒将红外光转换为哺乳动物眼睛可见的波长，适用于人类和老鼠。实验显示，佩戴这种隐形眼镜的小鼠能够感知红外光，并选择黑暗环境。而在人类测试中，参与者能够准确识别闪烁的红外信号和感知红外光方向。此外，通过调整纳米颗粒，还可以区分不同波长的红外光，并可能帮助色盲患者。尽管目前分辨率有限，研究团队还开发了配套的眼镜系统以提高分辨率。这项技术有望应用于安全、救援、加密等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： infrared contact lenses（红外接触镜）的科学研究及其潜在应用和挑战

不同观点：
• [az09mugen] 认为该研究结果出乎意料但很有趣，并对这种技术的实际应用表示好奇，尤其是它能如何被使用。
• [vintermann] 以幽默的方式表达了对在老鼠身上使用接触镜实验的惊讶，暗示其实验操作的难度。
• [greatgib] 关注使用者的体验，担心这种技术可能导致即使闭上眼睛也无法真正从视觉上得到休息。
• [jokethrowaway] 认为这项技术虽然是一个好的开始，但距离实际应用还有很长时间，并提到其他类似技术（如Ocumetics）的缓慢进展，甚至暗示可能存在商业阻碍。
• [4gotunameagain] 认为标题有夸大成分（点击诱饵），但承认该技术仍属于非常前沿的科学研究，目前功能有限，仅能检测特定光源的红外辐射。
• [fractallyte] 引用了科幻小说《Sinister Barrier》作为类比，半开玩笑地暗示如果研究人员开始神秘死亡，可能意味着这项研究触及了某些危险领域。

补充讨论：
• 该技术应用前景的讨论是核心，尤其是对实际生活的影响和可能遇到的商业化阻碍。[jokethrowaway] 的评论特别提到了类似技术的漫长测试周期，暗示红外接触镜可能也会面临类似问题。
• 争议的焦点似乎并不在于技术本身的可行性，而在于其实际应用的潜力和时间表。不同评论者对技术普及时间的预期存在分歧。
• 部分评论者如[fractallyte] 提到了科幻作品中的类似情境，暗示对技术可能带来的伦理或安全问题的担忧。
• 使用体验和潜在的生理或心理影响也被提出作为讨论要点，尤其是[greatgib] 对无法从视觉上得到休息的担忧。

Neuroscientists and materials scientists have created contact lenses that enable infrared vision in both humans and mice by converting infrared light into visible light. Unlike infrared night vision goggles, the contact lenses,
described in the journal
Cell
, do not require a power source—and they enable the wearer to perceive multiple infrared wavelengths. Because they're transparent, users can see both infrared and visible light simultaneously, though infrared vision was enhanced when participants had their eyes closed.
"Our research opens up the potential for noninvasive wearable devices to give people super-vision," says senior author Tian Xue, a neuroscientist at the University of Science and Technology of China. "There are many potential applications right away for this material. For example, flickering infrared light could be used to transmit information in security, rescue, encryption or anti-counterfeiting settings."
The contact lens technology uses nanoparticles that absorb infrared light and convert it into wavelengths that are visible to mammalian eyes (e.g.,
electromagnetic radiation
in the 400–700 nm range). The nanoparticles specifically enable the detection of "near-infrared light," which is infrared light in the 800–1600 nm range, just beyond what humans can already see.
The team previously showed that these nanoparticles enable infrared vision in mice when injected into the retina, but they wanted to design a less invasive option.
To create the contact lenses, the team combined the nanoparticles with flexible, nontoxic polymers that are used in standard soft contact lenses. After showing that the contact lenses were nontoxic, they tested their function in both humans and mice.
Preparation procedures for infrared contacts. Credit: Sheng Wang
They found that contact lens-wearing mice displayed behaviors suggesting that they could see infrared wavelengths. For example, when the mice were given the choice of a dark box and an infrared-illuminated box, contact-wearing mice chose the dark box whereas contact-less mice showed no preference.
The mice also showed physiological signals of
infrared vision
: the pupils of contact-wearing
mice
constricted in the presence of infrared light, and brain imaging revealed that infrared light caused their visual processing centers to light up.
In humans, the infrared contact lenses enabled participants to accurately detect flashing morse code-like signals and to perceive the direction of incoming infrared light.
"It's totally clear-cut: without the contact lenses, the subject cannot see anything, but when they put them on, they can clearly see the flickering of the infrared light," said Xue.
"We also found that when the subject closes their eyes, they're even better able to receive this flickering information, because near-infrared light penetrates the eyelid more effectively than
visible light
, so there is less interference from visible light."
Researcher places infrared contacts in participant's eyes. Credit: Yuqian Ma, Yunuo Chen, Hang Zhao
An additional tweak to the contact lenses allows users to differentiate between different spectra of infrared light by engineering the nanoparticles to color-code different infrared wavelengths. For example,
infrared wavelengths
of 980 nm were converted to blue light, wavelengths of 808 nm were converted to
green light
, and wavelengths of 1,532 nm were converted to red light.

In addition to enabling wearers to perceive more detail within the
infrared spectrum
, these color-coding nanoparticles could be modified to help color-blind people see wavelengths that they would otherwise be unable to detect.
"By converting red visible light into something like green visible light, this technology could make the invisible visible for color-blind people," says Xue.
Because the contact lenses have limited ability to capture fine details (due to their close proximity to the retina, which causes the converted light particles to scatter), the team also developed a wearable glass system using the same nanoparticle technology, which enabled participants to perceive higher-resolution infrared information.

44069751.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种由中国科技大学研究人员开发的 infrared（红外线）隐形眼镜，它可以在无需电源的情况下将红外光转换为可见光，使佩戴者在黑暗中甚至闭眼时也能看到红外线。这种技术利用纳米颗粒将红外光转换为哺乳动物眼睛可见的波长，适用于人类和老鼠。实验显示，佩戴这种隐形眼镜的小鼠能够感知红外光，并选择黑暗环境。而在人类测试中，参与者能够准确识别闪烁的红外信号和感知红外光方向。此外，通过调整纳米颗粒，还可以区分不同波长的红外光，并可能帮助色盲患者。尽管目前分辨率有限，研究团队还开发了配套的眼镜系统以提高分辨率。这项技术有望应用于安全、救援、加密等领域。

data.title: Tallest Wooden Wind Turbine
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一家公司建造木制风力涡轮机塔，实现净零风能的可能性。传统风力涡轮机塔通常由钢材制成，而该公司采用木材，这种可再生材料不仅能减少碳排放，还能加速风能产业的可持续发展。文章强调了木制塔的创新性和环保优势，展示了其如何推动绿色能源的未来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电实现净零排放的可行性及其相关技术材料选择

不同观点：
• [sebstefan] 认为风力发电的净零排放是一个不存在的伪问题，基于全生命周期的排放评估显示，风力涡轮机运行5.3个月后即可抵消其生产、安装、维护和处置所产生的排放。其他研究也得出相似结论。
• [jbms] 提出使用Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL) 材料替代钢材建造风力涡轮机塔，认为LVL在强度重量比和成本上优于钢材，并可能使塔更高。
• [aqme28] 对“净零”的具体含义提出疑问，质疑是否仅指材料和建造过程的净零排放，并认为风力涡轮机整体应为负排放。
• [kieranmaine] 引用播客观点，指出风力涡轮机无法像太阳能和电池一样通过缩小体积来降低成本，因为其组件需要规模效应，并讨论了运输和成本问题。
• [Bric3d] 认为风力涡轮机的生态问题主要在于叶片而非塔，建议关注叶片方面的改进。
• [svantana] 质疑风力涡轮机塔为何采用空心锥形圆筒设计，建议考虑桁架/网格结构以提高质量强度比。
• [bjourne] 指出历史上多次尝试用木材替代钢材均未成功，质疑此次是否会有不同结果。

补充讨论：
• [norome] 提出风力涡轮机外观设计问题，希望其外观更接近传统风车。
• [rcpt] 表达对风力涡轮机的喜爱，不理解对其的负面看法。
• [calmbonsai] 认为塔的建设和材料成本在整体风力发电系统中占比小，关键问题在于叶片的模块化和运输，而非塔的设计。
• [lupusreal] 幽默地认为木制风力涡轮机应称为风车。
• [carlosjobim] 对现代北欧工程项目选择表示质疑，认为一些项目看似聪明实则无意义，并指出项目资金来源于欧盟资助。

争议焦点：
• 风力涡轮机净零排放是否为伪问题，全生命周期排放评估是否可信。
• 风力涡轮机塔材料选择及其设计优化，钢材与木材的优劣对比。
• 风力涡轮机关键技术挑战在于塔的材料和设计还是叶片的模块化和运输。

data.title: KumoRFM: A Foundation Model for In-Context Learning on Relational Data
data.author: cliffly
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为KumoRFM的关系基础模型（RFM），专为结构化关系数据上的预测任务设计。与传统机器学习方法不同，KumoRFM无需针对特定数据或任务进行训练，即可在多种关系数据库的预测任务中提供准确预测。它采用预测查询语言（PQL）作为输入，能够处理诸如回归、分类和链接预测等任务。KumoRFM通过将关系数据库映射为时序异质图，利用表格不变编码方案和新型关系图变换器在多表间进行推理。其核心优势在于利用上下文学习，无需针对新任务或数据重新训练模型，且在多项评估中表现优于传统方法和监督学习模型。此外，KumoRFM在速度上也显著优于传统方法。

44070532.article_content:
Foundation Models (FMs) have completely taken over unstructured data domains like natural language and images, delivering significant advances in performance across tasks with little to no task-specific training. Yet structured and semi-structured relational data, which represent some of the most valuable information assets, largely miss out on this AI wave. To use AI on relational data, practitioners still use conventional machine learning approaches and build per-task and per-dataset specific models that require significant development and tuning time.
We present
KumoRFM
, a
Relational Foundation Model (RFM)
capable of making accurate predictions over relational databases across a wide range of predictive tasks without requiring data or task-specific training. KumoRFM extends principles of in-context learning to the multi-table relational graph setting. The model employs a table-invariant encoding scheme and a novel Relational Graph Transformer to reason within arbitrary multi-modal data across tables.
Through extensive evaluation on the
RelBench
benchmark, covering 30 predictive tasks across seven domains, we show that, on average, KumoRFM outperforms both the de-facto gold-standard of feature engineering as well as end-to-end supervised deep learning approaches by 2% to 8% across three different task types. When fine-tuned on a specific task, KumoRFM can improve its performance further by 10% to 30% on average. Most importantly, KumoRFM is orders of magnitude faster than conventional approaches that rely on supervised training.
Relational Foundation Models (RFMs)
Relational data is typically stored as structured tables in data warehouses and represents entities such as user records, transaction histories, supply chain interactions, product catalogs, financial ledgers, and health records. This data is commonly used for predictive questions like: "Is a given transaction fraudulent?", "What item is a user likely to interact with next?", "Will a user discontinue service?", or "What will be the sales of a product next quarter?"
Key capabilities of Relational Foundation Models.
Creating a foundation model for relational data presents unique challenges. Such a model needs to effectively learn across complex database schemas with an arbitrary number of tables and columns and handle the inherent heterogeneity of column types, which often have divergent semantic meanings. Several open questions had to be addressed:
What should a foundation model for relational data be capable of?
Can it generalize to new databases and tasks it has never been trained on?
Can it provide accurate predictions from a few in-context examples?
What architectural design is necessary to handle relational complexity?
What data is needed to train such a model effectively?
What is KumoRFM?
KumoRFM is a foundation model built for predictive tasks on structured, relational data, and draws from two key research areas: representation learning over relational databases and the emerging field of foundation models for structured data.
KumoRFM accepts as input a query written in a domain-specific language called
Predictive Query Language (PQL)
, which is similar in syntax to SQL but focused on defining prediction problems rather than data manipulation operations.
Mapping from predictive queries to task types. The aggregation scheme and the semantic type of the target column uniquely determine the underlying machine learning task.
Each PQL query defines the target variable to predict, the set of entities for which predictions should be made, and any filters or aggregation functions (e.g.,
FIRST
,
COUNT
,
SUM
,
LIST_DISTINCT
). Supported tasks include regression, binary classification, multi-class and multi-label classification, and link prediction. Once a query is submitted, KumoRFM retrieves relevant data from the underlying relational database and automatically generates context examples—labeled subgraphs that capture the relationships and historical patterns relevant to the prediction task. These are then used by the model to reason about the current query.
The system does not require task-specific training. Instead, it applies in-context learning at inference time by sampling from the historical data stored in the database. This allows it to handle new datasets or tasks without retraining the underlying model.
KumoRFM Under the Hood: Architecture and Design
KumoRFM operates on relational databases by internally converting them into temporal, heterogeneous graphs. Each table in the database is treated as a distinct node type, and rows in the tables become nodes. Foreign key relationships define the edges between nodes. Each node can carry multi-modal information such as numerical values, categories, timestamps, text, or vector embeddings.
Overview of the KumoRFM architecture.

A powerful real-time
in-context label generator
that dynamically curates task-specific context labels for any entit

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于某款早餐麦片的成分、形状及其数学与科学分析

不同观点：
• **关于麦片成分的健康担忧：**
  - [azalemeth] 引用营养数据和学术研究，指出该麦片含有高糖和高碳水化合物，且包含有潜在健康风险的食品添加剂BHT（丁基羟基甲苯）。根据其引用的研究，BHT在一定剂量下可能对生殖系统和肝脏有不良影响，尤其是在儿童中可能超出每日允许摄入量。因此，该评论者选择避免食用该产品，倾向于更健康的早餐选择（如吐司和燕麦）。

• **关于形状的数学讨论：**
  - [Sniffnoy] 提出可以使用等周不等式来简化对麦片形状的数学分析，而不是进行手动计算。他认为提到等周不等式能更好地解释形状优化问题。
  - [munchler] 指出球体因其表面积最小，不利于增加麦片表面的糖霜覆盖量，因此认为其他形状可能更优。
  - [throwawaymaths] 则反驳称，球形实际上是传递糖霜的完美形状，因为环形（torus）的内部可能不会接触舌头，从而浪费糖霜。
  - [bargle0] 补充说，球形可以最小化麦片的潮湿速度，因此从防潮角度看，球形也是有优势的。

• **关于营销和幽默的讨论：**
  - [Jabrov] 对凯洛格公司对消费者幽默的回应表示失望，认为其回复是公式化的，没有真正理解或欣赏消费者的幽默。
  - [jskelly] 引用了1980年代桂格燕麦公司的一个类似营销案例，提到当时声称某麦片角色发明了可以在地球和外太空使用的时间装置，以此来讽刺当前凯洛格的营销手段。

• **关于麦片形状的哲学讨论：**
  - [viccis] 以幽默的方式质疑，如果一个数学讨论没有用LaTeX排版，是否还能算作正式的数学研究，暗示对数学讨论形式的要求。
  - [d--b] 提出了“甜甜圈 vs 甜甜圈洞”的辩论，认为与传统的扁平麦片相比，这两种形状在糖霜覆盖方面都是退步，指责凯洛格在产品质量上的“劣化”。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点：** 主要集中在麦片的形状是否能有效传递糖霜，以及这种营销声称是否合理。此外，健康风险和成分分析也引发了对该产品是否值得购买的讨论。

data.title: Digital Payment System GNU Taler Gets Green Light to Operate in Switzerland
data.author: janandonly
data.article_summary: GNU Taler，一种注重隐私保护的数字支付系统，已获准在瑞士运营。该系统由自由软件基金会开发，旨在提供安全、匿名的交易方式，同时确保符合法律要求的透明度。通过瑞士的批准，GNU Taler将在该国开展业务，为用户提供一种兼顾隐私和合规的支付选择。这一进展标志着该系统在欧洲市场的进一步扩展，有助于提升数字支付的安全性和隐私保护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[欧盟新反洗钱法规对金融隐私工具（如Gnu Tallerc）的影响及竞争]

不同观点：
• [aitchnyu] 认为欧盟新的反洗钱法规可能会对Gnu Tallerc等工具产生影响，询问该法规是否会部分或完全限制这类工具的功能。这表明了对监管环境收紧的担忧，可能对隐私工具的未来使用产生限制。

• [jxjnskkzxxhx] 对Gnu Tallerc的具体功能感到困惑，并将其与传统银行应用进行比较。他们质疑Gnu Tallerc是否仅提供了隐私保护和匿名支付的优势，并提出银行可以轻松复制这些功能的观点。这反映了对该工具实际独特性的疑问，以及对银行是否会提供类似服务的猜测。

• [herbst] 则指出Twint（瑞士的一个支付系统）已经在市场上广泛应用，并提供了类似的功能，质疑Gnu Tallerc如何能在已经饱和的市场中竞争。这表明了对市场竞争环境的关注，以及对新工具能否成功的怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Gnu Tallerc是否提供了显著优于传统银行应用的独特功能，尤其是在隐私保护和匿名支付方面。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是欧盟新反洗钱法规的潜在影响，这可能会改变Gnu Tallerc等隐私工具的运作方式和可用性。

• 市场竞争也是一个重要议题，特别是如何在已有类似服务的市场中定位和推广新工具。Twint作为一个成熟的市场竞争者，被认为是一个难以逾越的障碍。

总结来看，讨论围绕着Gnu Tallerc的功能独特性、与银行应用的比较、以及在当前监管和市场环境下的可行性展开。各方对隐私保护的实际需求和市场竞争力有不同的看法，同时也关注法规变化可能带来的影响。

data.author: marklit
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用Depth Anything V2深度估算模型处理Maxar卫星提供的2025年曼谷卫星图像的过程。Depth Anything V2由TikTok和香港大学开发，使用了约60万张合成标注图像和超过6200万张真实未标注图像进行训练。作者使用高性能工作站（AMD Ryzen 9 9950X CPU, 96GB DDR5 RAM等）运行Ubuntu 24 LTS环境，通过Windows 11 Pro的Linux子系统进行操作。文中详细描述了安装所需软件和依赖的步骤，并下载了模型的最大版本（335.3M参数）。卫星图像来自Maxar的开放数据项目，作者选择了曼谷Chatuchak区的一部分图像进行深度估计分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新技术（自动生成3D模型的潜力应用）

不同观点：
• [qoez] 认为该技术可能有很酷的应用，但目前想不出具体的例子。虽然计算阴影等可能有用，但很多地方（尤其是城市区域）已经有3D建筑，不过农村地区可能是个例外。
  
• [actinium226] 提到自己曾做过类似的项目，但只是作为学习神经网络的工具，并没有找到令人信服的实际应用场景。对文章作者或模型开发者是否找到实际应用表示好奇。
  
• [sandspar] 提出该技术是否会为Google Earth和Microsoft Flight Simulator等平台提供更多世界城市的3D模型，特别是在目前这些平台上3D模型仅限于少数城市或富裕国家。同时，对地形（如山脉）的精确建模也提出了疑问，因为目前很多地形高度信息是基于推测的。

补充讨论：
• 技术的潜在应用场景仍不明确，评论者普遍对其实际用途持不确定态度，但认为在农村地区的3D建模和现有平台的改进上可能有价值。
• 具体应用场景的讨论集中在Google Earth和Microsoft Flight Simulator等已有平台的改进，尤其是3D城市和地形模型的精确性。
• 争议焦点在于该技术是否真的能找到广泛的实际应用，或仅限于特定领域如农村建模或教育用途。

44049926.article_content:
Satellites Spotting Depth
Depth Anything V2
is a depth estimation model that was released last year. It was developed by a team from TikTok and the University of Hong Kong (HKU). Almost ~600K synthetic, labelled images and over 62M real, unlabelled images were used in its training.
In this post, I'll run Depth Anything V2's largest model against Maxar's satellite imagery 2025 of Bangkok, Thailand.
My Workstation
I'm using a 5.7 GHz AMD Ryzen 9 9950X CPU. It has 16 cores and 32 threads and 1.2 MB of L1, 16 MB of L2 and 64 MB of L3 cache. It has a liquid cooler attached and is housed in a spacious, full-sized Cooler Master HAF 700 computer case.
The system has 96 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 4,800 MT/s and a 5th-generation, Crucial T700 4 TB NVMe M.2 SSD which can read at speeds up to 12,400 MB/s. There is a heatsink on the SSD to help keep its temperature down. This is my system's C drive.
The system is powered by a 1,200-watt, fully modular Corsair Power Supply and is sat on an ASRock X870E Nova 90 Motherboard.
I'm running Ubuntu 24 LTS via Microsoft's Ubuntu for Windows on Windows 11 Pro. In case you're wondering why I don't run a Linux-based desktop as my primary work environment, I'm still using an Nvidia GTX 1080 GPU which has better driver support on Windows and I use ArcGIS Pro from time to time which only supports Windows natively.
Installing Prerequisites
I'm running Esri's
ArcGIS Pro 3.5
. This version is their latest and was released last week.
I'll also use Python 3.12.3 in this post.
$
sudo
add-apt-repository
ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
$
sudo
apt
update
$
sudo
apt
install
\
python3-pip
\
python3.12-venv
I'll clone DepthAnything's v2 repo.
$
git
clone
https://github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2
\
~/Depth-Anything-V2
I'll set up a Python Virtual Environment and install Depth Anything's dependencies.
$
python3
-m
venv
~/.depth_anything_v2
$
source
~/.depth_anything_v2/bin/activate
$
python3
-m
pip
install
\
-r
~/Depth-Anything-V2/requirements.txt
DepthAnything v2 has three different pre-trained models available. I'll download their largest 335.3M-parameter model that has a footprint of ~1.3 GB.
$
mkdir
-p
~/Depth-Anything-V2/checkpoints
$
cd
~/Depth-Anything-V2/checkpoints
$
wget
'https://huggingface.co/depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Large/resolve/main/depth_anything_v2_vitl.pth?download=true'
Maxar's Bangkok Satellite Imagery
Maxar have an
open data programme
that I wrote a post on a few years ago. I later
revisited
this feed last month after the earthquake struck Myanmar and Thailand.
I'll be using two images from this feed in this post. The first image covers part of the Chatuchak district and includes Ratchadaphisek Road which has several tall towers along it.
The image is a GeoTIFF pyramid containing a 17408x17408-pixel JPEG covering an area ~5.2 x 4.2 KM. The image was captured on February 14th by Maxar's WorldView 3 satellite at a resolution of 38cm.
$
wget
https://maxar-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/events/Earthquake-Myanmar-March-2025/ard/47/122022102203/2025-02-14/10400100A4C67F00-visual.tif
This is the image below in relation to its surrounding area in Bangkok.
Below I've zoomed into Ratchadaphisek Road where you can see the tall towers.

• 技术的潜在应用场景仍不明确，评论者普遍对其实际用途持不确定态度，但认为在农村地区的3D建模和现有平台的改进上可能有价值。

data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PostgreSQL的扩展与使用，特别是在大规模应用中的实践和挑战

不同观点：
• **对演讲的积极评价**：[samwillis]认为演讲内容对很多需要扩展Postgres的小团队非常有帮助，尤其是强调了读写分离和读副本的扩展策略。演讲的重点是通过使用这些策略，Postgres可以在高读取负载下扩展，这对大多数应用来说已经足够。
• **对演讲的消极评价**：[williamdclt]认为演讲内容较为基础，提到的扩展方法在更小规模的场景下也是常识。同时，他认为演讲中提到的某些功能请求并不新颖，且有些问题可以通过现有方法解决，尽管这些方法可能并不完美。
• **对自托管与云服务的权衡**：[tux3]认为自托管Postgres有其吸引力，尤其是在需要高级功能和超级用户权限时，但也承认这可能带来一些风险和挑战。[belter]则认为，许多扩展问题可以通过使用AWS和Aurora Postgres来解决。
• **对ORM的批评**：[VWWHFSfQ]强烈反对使用ORM，认为它们会导致低效的查询，并限制了Postgres的强大功能。建议直接编写SQL以获得最佳性能。
• **对物理复制与逻辑复制的讨论**：[davidkuennen]在考虑是否切换到逻辑复制以减少跨区域的出口成本，并提到Postgres 17中的改进。
• **对OpenAI技术选择的质疑**：[philosophty]质疑OpenAI雇佣缺乏操作经验的人员，并认为Postgres并不适合他们的需求，暗示他们的技术选择不够理想。

补充讨论：
• **功能请求与现有解决方案**：[cryptonector]指出，使用`EVENT TRIGGER`可以实现对DDL操作的记录，并提供了Aquameta作为参考。[williamdclt]则认为，某些未文档化的方法（如设置`indisvalid`字段）不应被视为正式功能。
• **对索引管理的建议**：[williamdclt]和[redwood]都提到，通过监控视图确认索引的使用情况是一种解决方案，但不能完全解决所有问题。能够临时禁用索引以测试查询计划是更理想的选择。
• **对分片的建议**：[bhouston]强烈建议使用分片来解决数据库扩展问题，认为这是简单的解决方案，但演讲中并未采用。
• **对演讲标题的建议**：[airstrike]认为演讲标题应更明确地反映OpenAI的案例。
• **对开源社区贡献的期望**：[kabes]认为，像OpenAI这样资金充裕的公司不应只是请求开源社区添加功能，而应通过提交PR来贡献代码。

争议焦点：
• **演讲内容的实用性和新颖性**：一部分人认为演讲提供了有价值的实践经验，尤其是对小团队和内部开发者而言；另一部分人则认为内容基础且已为人熟知，缺乏新意。
• **Postgres在大规模应用中的适用性**：一些人认为Postgres通过适当的策略可以很好地扩展，另一些人则质疑其在大规模场景下的适用性，并建议使用其他工具或服务。

data.title: 'Turbocharged' Mitochondria Power Birds' Epic Migratory Journeys
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨鸟类如何通过线粒体的变化实现长距离迁徙。线粒体是细胞中的“能量工厂”，在迁徙季节，鸟类肌肉细胞中的线粒体数量、形状、效率和互联性会发生变化，从而提供额外能量。这些变化使鸟类能不间断飞行数千英里，如白冠雀和北极燕鸥。研究表明，这种生理变化由光周期触发，而非基因改变，显示了鸟类的“表型可塑性”。这一发现帮助科学家理解鸟类如何在迁徙中完成高强度、长时间的飞行壮举。

‘Turbocharged’ Mitochondria Power Birds’ Epic Migratory Journeys
By
Elizabeth Landau

Changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of organelles in the cells of flight muscles provide extra energy for birds’ continent-spanning feats.

How do small birds migrate long distances? Mitochondria are key.
Nan Cao for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Elizabeth Landau
Contributing Writer

W
eighing in at a single ounce, the white-crowned sparrow can fly 2,600 miles, from Mexico to Alaska, on its annual spring migration, sometimes traveling 300 miles in a single night. Arctic terns make even longer journeys of 10,000 miles and more from the Arctic Circle to Antarctica, while great snipes fly over food-poor deserts and seas, sometimes covering 4,200 miles in four days without stopping.
During migration season, many bird species become continent-spanning, high-endurance athletes. “They’re flapping their wings several times a second for up to eight hours at a time,” said
Soren Coulson
, who studies migration physiology at the University of Memphis. For humans, an equivalent feat — say, running nonstop without food, water or rest for days at a time — would be unimaginable.
“We were just amazed and interested in how can these birds fly for thousands of miles without stopping, at a really high intensity, when most of us can barely run a 5K,” said
Paulo Mesquita
, who studies mitochondrial physiology and muscle aging at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation.
Scientists have long been fascinated with the
physiological changes
that birds undergo before and during migration. Some birds eat so much fat before their journeys that they double in body weight. In some species, their hearts are enlarged to pump more blood, or their digestive tracts grow and then shrink. But researchers have only recently started to explore at a fundamental level how migratory birds get the energy required to keep themselves aloft for days on end without eating.
Last year, two independent groups published research that explored migratory bird physiology in the lab and field to probe what happens at the subcellular level that allows birds to cover vast distances. They both found answers in biology’s most fundamental engine: mitochondria.
Their studies show how small changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of mitochondria can have huge physiological consequences that contribute to birds’ long-duration, continent-spanning flights.
“Exercise physiologists study the mitochondria because they provide the energy needed to maintain healthy cells, to maintain proper cellular function — but also, just in general, the energy we need to exercise,” Mesquita said. “That energy is what fuels movement.”

To Paulo Mesquita, an exercise physiologist, mitochondria are the center of the universe.
Courtesy of Paulo Mesquita/OMRF
These pioneering studies on mitochondrial performance and bird migration highlight the fact that a seasonal response to changing light levels, not physical preparation, triggers crucial subcellular changes, said
Wendy Hood
, who studies physiological ecology at Auburn University in Alabama; Mesquita worked with her and other colleagues on these questions during his graduate studies.
Humans “have to train for a while before we start to see any changes in the performance of our mitochondria,” she said. With migratory birds, “it’s spring, they get the right light cycles, and their body starts producing more and better, or higher-quality, mitochondria.”
The recent work advances the idea that there are significant ways in which an organism can change, without modifying its underlying genetic makeup, in response to its environment, said
Scott McWilliams
, a professor of wildlife ecology and physiology at the University of Rhode Island who was not involved in either study. This “phenotypic flexibility” in birds has been shown to vary according to seasons and population, and these studies are some of the first to demonstrate this across species and subspecies at the mitochondrial level.
“Such a theme,” he said, “is centrally important for understanding how birds during migration accomplish their athletic feats.”

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ACME协议及其工具的复杂性、实现问题和安全性

不同观点：
• eadmund认为JSON在处理大整数时存在问题，导致需要额外的步骤来编码大整数，并对ACME规范的实现表示不满，认为其增加了不必要的复杂性。他还提到XML不如Canonical S-expressions理想。
• 1a527dd5对ACME工具的选择和使用体验进行了分享，提到在使用不同ACME客户端时遇到的挑战，并指出作者批评的可能是ACME规范本身，而非ACME概念或工具。
• liampulles支持作者提出的观点，认为协议的复杂性增加了开发者负担，并可能导致只有大公司才能满足互联网运行的规范要求。
• jeroenhd感觉到作者对协议和额外工作的厌恶，并建议使用轻量级ACME库来简化设置。
• sam_lowry_提到运营HTTP网站越来越难，因外部环境（如Whatsapp）对HTTPS的要求增加。
• neogodless分享了在实现HMAC签名时遇到的困难，尤其是在缺乏有效反馈的情况下调试脚本的问题。
• orion138偏离主话题，询问2025年推荐的域名注册商，显示出对域名管理工具的关注。
• matja认为虽然JOSE/JWK规范复杂，但整体流程是可行的，并分享了自己使用certbot的简化方法。
• tux3认为JOSE/JWK规范虽然复杂，但整体还在可接受范围内，认为base64url和JSON并不是最糟糕的实现选择。
• tialaramex详细解释了SAN的必要性和历史背景，指出其在X.500目录系统中的作用，并强调SAN使得证书解析更加可靠。
• z3t4提到在处理TXT记录和通配符域名时遇到的实际操作困难，尤其是DNS服务器的缓存机制带来的挑战。
• amiga386讨论了HTTPS和CA信任模型的必要性，指出证书更新频率的增加是为了提高安全性，并提到多种ACME客户端和证书颁发机构的选择。

data.title: Quantum Picturalism
data.author: mathgenius
data.article_summary: 《Quantum for Everyone》介绍了一种名为“Quantum Picturalism”（量子图像主义）的创新学习方法，旨在让量子教育变得更加 accessible 和直观。该方法由Bob Coecke和Stefano Gogioso在其著作《Quantum in Pictures》中提出，通过使用加减法和角度等简单数学概念，以视觉化方式解释复杂的量子理论，无需高等数学知识。量子图像主义的历史和发展历程展示了其逐步演变的过程，并且通过Discord社区和常见问题解答，帮助初学者轻松入门。这种方法使各个年龄层的学习者都能理解量子概念，降低了学习的难度，扩大了量子知识的受众范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ZX calculus及其在量子计算研究和教育中的应用

不同观点：
• [tmvphil] 认为ZX calculus是进行前沿研究（如误差修正和门编译）的有趣框架，但对于让更多大众理解量子计算而言，它显得过于抽象和复杂。他认为超过简单比喻（如“量子隐形传态就像拉一根绳子”）的图像化描述都非常难以理解和操作。他以实验量子计算博士的背景强调了这一点。
  
• [pentaphobe] 对ZX calculus与费曼图之间的关系感到好奇，并通过搜索找到了一些相关资料，分享了相关总结和原始论文的链接，但未深入讨论其教育意义或复杂性。

• [tlogan] 认为要真正理解量子物理，数学是唯一途径，主张“闭嘴计算”的方法。他还批评学术界使用复杂的符号和术语，认为这是故意让知识显得更难懂以显得“聪明”和“排外”。他比较了美国和前社会主义国家对概念命名的差异，指出后者使用更通俗的语言帮助学习。

• [baxtr] 引用了“量子图像主义”一词，指出这种通过视觉方式教授量子概念的方法可以降低学习的难度，并让更多人接触到这一领域，暗示ZX calculus或类似的图像化工具在教育中具有潜力。

补充讨论：
• tmvphil和baxtr的观点形成了直接的对比。前者认为ZX calculus的抽象性限制了其在普及教育中的应用，而后者认为图像化方法有助于降低学习门槛。
• tlogan的评论引入了学术界术语和命名惯例的问题，认为这可能是让量子物理显得难以接近的原因之一，并通过对比不同国家的命名方式提出了改进建议。
• pentaphobe的评论虽然主要是信息分享，但提供了进一步了解ZX calculus与费曼图关系的资源，为讨论提供了背景材料。

争议焦点：ZX calculus是否适合作为普及量子计算知识的工具。tmvphil认为其过于复杂，而baxtr则认为图像化方法有助于普及教育。

No complex math required.
Learn quantum concepts using just addition, subtraction, and angles.
Quantum ideas are often seen as intimidating, which can discourage people from exploring them. We make quantum education accessible by breaking down complex concepts into simple, visual learning experiences.
What is Quantum Picturalism?
Quantum Picturalism is a visual form of math that only requires addition, subtraction, and angles to depict quantum ideas. The approach uses “game-like” rules, and yet it’s rigorous enough for use by quantum experts around the world.
This empowers teachers and learners of all ages by making quantum math accessible and inclusive.
The term, “Quantum Picturalism” was coined to describe this unique approach of teaching quantum concepts visually, reducing intimidation and opening the field to broader audiences.

data.title: Remote Prompt Injection in Gitlab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft
data.author: chillax
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Legit研究团队在GitLab Duo中发现的远程提示注入漏洞，该漏洞可导致源代码泄露和HTML注入攻击。GitLab Duo是集成在GitLab中的人工智能助手，旨在帮助开发者进行代码建议、安全审查等任务。然而，研究发现，通过在合并请求、提交信息、问题描述和源代码中嵌入隐藏提示，攻击者可以操纵GitLab Duo，泄露私有项目的源代码，篡改代码建议，甚至泄露未公开的零日漏洞。

攻击者利用KaTeX、Base16等编码技巧隐藏提示，成功骗过系统。此外，由于GitLab Duo的响应采用Markdown格式并逐步渲染，攻击者可以注入恶意HTML，控制页面部分内容，发起网络攻击。GitLab已修复此问题，但文章详细解析了整个攻击链，展示了从提示注入到HTML注入的完整过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对大语言模型（LLM）应用中的安全问题，尤其是提示注入（prompt injection）和数据泄露问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• [cedws] 认为在提示注入问题解决之前，不会将LLM接入任何工具（如MCPs、IDEs、agents）。出于安全考虑，只会在有疑问时使用简单的提示框，并手动处理输出结果。

• [wunderwuzzi23] 对数据泄露问题表示关注，特别提到通过不受信任的第三方服务器（尤其是图像渲染）导致的数据泄露，这是常见的AI安全问题。他提到自己曾发现并记录了多个相关漏洞，包括GitHub Copilot Chat去年的类似漏洞。

• [aestetix] 以调侃的语气询问GitLab Duo是否可以运行Doom（一种游戏），暗示对GitLab Duo的功能和安全性存在质疑。

• [mdaniel] 批评GitLab允许Duo以系统用户身份运行是疯狂且不合理的做法，并建议使用个人访问令牌，甚至为Duo单独创建一个令牌，以替代赋予LLM读取所有仓库的权限。

• [nusl] 认为GitLab的修复措施看起来不太可靠，对GitLab的安全修复持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
- 提示注入和数据泄露是LLM应用中的两大主要安全问题，且这些问题在行业内广泛存在。
- 讨论中对GitLab的实现方式和安全修复措施存在较多质疑和批评，尤其是对LLM拥有过大权限的担忧。
- 不同的参与者对具体漏洞和安全隐患有实际案例和经验的分享，如[wunderwuzzi23]提到的GitHub Copilot Chat漏洞。
- 讨论中也涉及到对具体产品（如GitLab Duo）功能的质疑和讽刺。

44070626.article_content: Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Written by Omer Mayraz Published on May 22, 2025 Updated on May 22, 2025 In this article Sign up for our newsletter Get details on the vulnerabilities the Legit research team unearthed in GitLab Duo. TL;DR: A hidden comment was enough to make GitLab Duo leak private source code and inject untrusted HTML into its responses. GitLab patched the issue, and we’ll walk you through the full attack chain — which demonstrates five vulnerabilities from the 2025 OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Background GitLab Duo , the AI assistant integrated into GitLab and powered by Anthropic’s Claude, is designed to help developers with tasks like code suggestions, security reviews, and merge request analysis. But what if the same AI meant to secure your code could be manipulated into leaking it? That’s exactly what we uncovered: a remote prompt injection vulnerability that allows attackers to steal source code from private projects, manipulate code suggestions shown to other users, and even exfiltrate confidential, undisclosed zero-day vulnerabilities — all through GitLab Duo Chat. In this blog post, we break down how the attack works — from prompt injection to HTML injection — and walk through a real-world end-to-end exploit scenario. Manipulating GitLab Duo Through Hidden Prompts ( LLM01 ) We started by testing if GitLab Duo would respond to prompts planted inside source code. To our surprise, it did: This led us to a key question: Could we embed hidden instructions in different parts of a GitLab project and still influence Duo’s behavior? W e experimented by placing hidden prompts in: Merge Request (MR) descriptions and comments Commit messages Issue descriptions and comments Source code Every single one of these worked — GitLab Duo responded to the hidden prompts. Why? Because to generate helpful answers, Duo analyzes the entire context of the page, including comments, descriptions, and the source code — making it vulnerable to injected instructions hidden anywhere in that context. KaTex, Base16, and Invisible Text ( LLM08 ) To make prompts less detectable, we used encoding tricks: Unicode smuggling with ASCII Smuggler Base16-encoded payloads KaTeX rendering in white text (to ma ke prompts invisible inside GitLab’s website) For example, you can publish comments and descriptions in white text inside GitLab’s website by using this KaTeX format: More info about KaTeX can be found here: KaTeX – The fastest math typesetting library for the web . These hidden instructions were still picked up by Duo. AI Output You Shouldn’t Trust ( LLM09 ) This led to several high-impact behaviors: Manipulate Duo’s code suggestions - even instructing it to include a malicious JavaScript package within its recommended code. Present a malicious URL as safe in Duo’s response — leading the user to click it and land on a fake login page. Convince Duo to present a malicious merge request as safe, misleading reviewers. Take a look at this prompt: Duo followed this hidden prompt, casually suggesting malicious code to the user: HTML Injection: Turning Duo Into a Web Attack Vector ( LLM05 ) Duo also formats responses in Markdown, allowing rich content like URLs with custom labels: After some research, we were able to create a prompt that makes Duo present malicious URLs: Prompt is inside the source code, camouflaged as unicode inside a URL And then, something caught our eye. While experimenting with GitLab Duo’s responses, We noticed that its answers were rendered progressively - line by line - as they streamed in. Notice the style changes in the word “initialization”? This indicated that asynchronous markdown parsing was being used. That’s important because it means the markdown is interpreted and rendered into HTML before the full structure of the response is known. Streaming markdown rendering (as seen in Duo) works like this: Partial input arrives - the frontend starts rendering line by line. Sanitization and structure (e.g., is this a code block, paragraph, quote?) is applied as the content grows. If a malicious HTML tag is streamed before a code block starts, or outside fenced blocks, it may be treated as active HTML. This means that the AI answer - intended to be safe markdown - renders active HTML too early. At this point, we realized that we could already craft malicious Markdown URLs and have them displayed to the user. So we asked: what if the URL’s label itself contained raw HTML? If Duo renders responses in real time, the browser might interpret that HTML before any proper sanitization kicks in. By injecting raw HTML into content that’s rendered live, we could gain control over parts of the page — including the ability to insert elements like tags that trigger automatic HTTP requests to attacker-controlled servers. data.title: Ship footage captures sound of Titan sub imploding
data.author: coryfklein
data.article_summary: 2023年6月，Oceangate的泰坦潜水器在探访泰坦尼克号残骸时发生内爆，造成船上五名人员死亡。BBC纪录片《内爆：泰坦尼克号潜水器灾难》披露了事故发生时的视频，当时支持船上的泰坦CEO拉什的妻子听到一声巨响，并问道：“那是什么声音？”美国海岸警卫队调查显示，内爆发生时的声音被误认为是潜水器正常操作的声响。其实，泰坦的碳纤维船体在一年前的下潜中已开始分层，最终导致灾难。专家曾警告泰坦的设计存在严重问题，但未进行独立安全评估。事故后，残骸散落在大西洋海底，调查发现包括拉什的衣物等物品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于潜水器失事前短信传递时间的合理性及通信设备的生存能力

不同观点：
• [fidotron] 认为文本消息传递的时间不合理，质疑官方的解释。他认为在潜水器发生内爆之前发送的短信，传递到母船的时间比声音（内爆声）到达的时间还要长，这一点令人怀疑。他要求官方给出合理解释。

• [fidotron] 同时提出了一种可能性，即通信设备可能在事故中幸存下来，并在事故后传递了缓存的消息。这意味着设备可能是可恢复的，暗示了官方可能尚未完全披露设备的状况。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于短信传递时间与内爆声传递时间的不匹配，引发了对官方解释的怀疑。
• [fidotron] 提出了通信设备幸存的可能性，并对设备的潜在可恢复性进行了推测，这为进一步的调查和技术分析提供了方向。
• 该评论还暗示了对信息透明度和事故调查深度的关注，认为可能存在未披露的技术细节或发现。

Stockton Rush's wife Wendy asks "what's that bang?" in footage that appears in new BBC documentary
The moment that Oceangate's Titan submersible was lost has been revealed in footage recorded on the sub's support ship.
Titan imploded about 90 minutes into a descent to see the wreck of the Titanic in June 2023, killing all five people on board.
The passengers had paid Oceangate to see the ship, which lies 3,800m down.
On board were Oceangate's CEO Stockton Rush, British explorer Hamish Harding, veteran French diver Paul Henri Nargeolet, the British-Pakistani businessman Shahzada Dawood and his 19-year-old son Suleman.
The BBC has had unprecedented access to the US Coast Guard's (USCG) investigation for a documentary, Implosion: The Titanic Sub Disaster.
The footage was recently obtained by the USCG and shows Wendy Rush, the wife of Mr Rush, hearing the sound of the implosion while watching on from the sub's support ship and asking: "What was that bang?"
The video has been presented as evidence to the USCG Marine Board of Investigation, which has spent the last two years looking into the sub's catastrophic failure.
The documentary also reveals the carbon fibre used to build the submersible started to break apart a year before the fatal dive.
Titan's support ship was with the sub while it was diving in the Atlantic Ocean. The video shows Mrs Rush, who was a director of Oceangate with her husband, sitting in front of a computer that was used to send and receive text messages from Titan.
When the sub reaches a depth of about 3,300m, a noise that sounds like a door slamming is heard. Mrs Rush is seen to pause then look up and ask other Oceangate crew members what the noise was.
Within moments she then receives a text message from the sub saying it had dropped two weights, which seems to have led her to mistakenly think the dive was proceeding as expected.
The USCG says the noise was in fact the sound of Titan imploding. However, the text message, which must have been sent just before the sub failed, took longer to reach the ship than the sound of the implosion.
All five people on board Titan died instantly.
Prior to the fatal dive, warnings had been raised by deep sea experts and some former Oceangate employees about Titan's design. One described it as
an "abomination" and said the disaster was "inevitable"
.
Titan had never undergone an independent safety assessment, known as certification, and a key concern was that its hull - the main body of the sub where the passengers sat - was made of layers of carbon fibre mixed with resin.
The USCG says it has now identified the moment the hull started to fail.
Carbon fibre is a highly unusual material for a deep sea submersible because it is unreliable under pressure. A known problem is that the layers of carbon fibre can separate, a process called delamination.
The USCG believes that the carbon fibre layers of the hull started to break apart during a dive to the Titanic, which took place a year before the disaster - the 80th dive that Titan had made.
Passengers on board reported hearing a loud bang as the sub made its way back to the surface. They said that at the time Mr Rush said that this noise was the sub shifting in its frame.
But the USCG says the data collected from sensors fitted to Titan shows that the bang was caused by delamination.
"Delamination at dive 80 was the beginning of the end," said Lieutenant Commander Katie Williams from USCG.
"And everyone that stepped onboard the Titan after dive 80 was risking their life."
Titan took passengers on three more dives in the summer of 2022 - two to the Titanic and one to a nearby reef, before it failed on its next deep dive, in June 2023.
US Coastguard
The flaws of Titan's carbon fibre shell were shown to the inquiry
Businessman Oisin Fanning was onboard Titan for the last two dives before the disaster.
"If you're asking a simple question: 'Would I go again knowing what I know now?' - the answer is no," he told BBC News.
"A lot of people would not have gone. Very intelligent people who lost their lives, who, had they had all the facts, would not have made that journey."
Deep sea explorer Victor Vescovo said he had grave misgivings about Titan and that he had told people that diving in the sub was like playing Russian roulette.
"I myself warned people away from getting into that submersible. I specifically told them that it was simply a matter of time before it failed catastrophically. I told Stockton Rush himself that I believed that."
After the sub imploded, its mangled wreckage was discovered scattered across the sea floor of the Atlantic.
The USCG has described the process of sifting through the recovered debris - and said clothing from Mr Rush had been found, as well as business cards and stickers of the Titanic.
Supplied via Reuters / AFP

data.title: The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source
data.author: pentagrama
data.article_summary: 2025年5月19日，微软宣布Windows Subsystem for Linux（WSL）正式开源。这一成果是多年努力的结果，WSL代码已在GitHub上的Microsoft/WSL仓库中开放，社区可以下载、修改和添加新功能。WSL由多个组件构成，包括命令行工具、服务进程、Linux init进程以及文件共享实现等。尽管部分组件如Lxcore.sys仍未开源，但其他如WSLg和WSL2的Linux内核早已开放。WSL最初在2016年发布，经历了从WSL 1到WSL 2的演变，逐渐支持GPU、图形应用和systemd等功能。2021年，WSL从Windows代码库中分离并迁移至微软商店独立发布，最新版本为WSL 2.5.7。开源WSL旨在加速其发展，以更好地满足社区需求。

44031385.article_content:
Microsoft Build
May 19, 2025
The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source
By
Pierre Boulay
Today we’re very excited to announce the open-source release of the Windows Subsystem for Linux. This is the result of a multiyear effort to prepare for this, and a great closure to the first ever issue raised on the Microsoft/WSL repo:
Will this be Open Source? · Issue #1 · microsoft/WSL
.
That means that the code that powers WSL is now available on GitHub at
Microsoft/WSL
and open sourced to the community! You can download WSL and build it from source, add new fixes and features and participate in WSL’s active development.
WSL component overview
WSL is made of a set of distribution components. Some run in Windows, and some run inside the WSL 2 virtual machine. Here’s an overview of WSL’s architecture:
WSL’s code can be broken up into these main areas:
Command line executables that are the entry points to interact with WSL
wsl.exe, wslconfig.exe and wslg.exe
The WSL service that starts the WSL VM, starts distros, mounts file access shares and more
wslservice.exe
Linux init and daemon processes, binaries that run in Linux to provide WSL functionality
init for start up, gns for networking, localhost for port forwarding, etc.
File sharing Linux files to Windows with WSL’s plan9 server implementation
plan9
Head over to
https://wsl.dev
to learn more about each component.
This comes as an addition to the already open sourced WSL components:
microsoft/wslg: Enabling the Windows Subsystem for Linux to include support for Wayland and X server related scenarios
microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel: The source for the Linux kernel used in Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2)
The following components are still part of the Windows image and are not open sourced at this time:
Lxcore.sys, the kernel side driver that powers WSL 1
P9rdr.sys and p9np.dll, which runs the “\\wsl.localhost” filesystem redirection (from Windows to Linux)
Why open source now? A bit of history…
WSL was first announced at BUILD back in 2016 and first shipped with the Windows 10 Anniversary update.
At that time WSL was based on a pico process provider, lxcore.sys, which enabled Windows to natively run ELF executables, and implement Linux syscalls inside the Windows kernel. This eventually became what we today know as “WSL 1”, which WSL still supports.
Over time it became clear that the best way to provide optimal compatibility with native Linux was to rely on the Linux kernel itself. WSL 2 was born, and first announced in 2019.
As the community behind WSL grew, WSL gained more features such as GPU support, graphical applications support (via wslg) and support for systemd.
It eventually became clear that to keep up with the growing community and feature requests, WSL had to move faster, and ship separately from Windows. That’s why in 2021 we separated WSL from the Windows codebase, and moved it to its own codebase. This new WSL first shipped as version 0.47.1 to the Microsoft Store, in July 2021. At the time, only Windows 11 was supported, and the package was marked as preview, only recommended to users that wanted to experience the latest and greatest of WSL.
We continued to develop this new “WSL package” until it was ready for general availability. That happened November of 2022, with WSL 1.0.0, which added support for Windows 10 and was the first “stable” release of this new WSL.
From there we kept on improving WSL, with the objective of fully transitioning all users to this new WSL package, and away from the WSL component that shipped with Windows. Windows 11 24H2 was the first Windows build that moved users from the “built-in” WSL to the “new” WSL package. We kept wsl.exe in the Windows image, so it could download the latest package on demand to make the transition easier.
As we kept on improving WSL, we eventually hit another milestone: WSL 2.0.0 (What are the three hardest problems in computer science? Off by one errors and naming things!).
WSL 2.0.0 introduced major improvements such as mirrored networking, DNS tunneling, session 0 support, proxy support, firewall support and more.
And that’s the milestone we’re still building on today! At the time of writing this article, WSL
2.5.7
is the latest available version out of our
nine pages of Github releases
since 0.47.1 4 years ago !
The community behind WSL
Over the years we’ve been incredibly lucky to have a strong community supporting WSL from day 1. We’ve been blessed with people sharing their knowledge, and spending countless hours to help track down bugs, find the best ways to implement new features and improve WSL.
WSL could never have been what it is today without its community. Even without access to WSL’s source code, people have been able to make major contributions that lead to what WSL is now.
This is why we’re incredibly excited to open-source WSL today. We’ve seen how much the community has contributed to WSL without access to the source code, and we can’t wait to see how WSL will evolve now t

data.title: Show HN: Samchika – A Java Library for Fast, Multithreaded File Processing
data.author: mprataps
data.article_summary: Samchika 是一个专为 Java 设计的高性能、多线程文件处理库，专注于并行处理大文件，具有快速和轻量的特点。它提供简单易用的 API，支持批量处理、运行时统计可选，并适用于日志分析、ETL操作、大文本处理等多种场景。该库在多核系统中表现出显著的性能提升，相比传统的 BufferedReader 方法，处理速度更快，内存消耗可控。Samchika 基于 MIT 许可证开源，欢迎贡献和使用。安装可通过 Maven 或 Gradle 进行，并提供了详细的示例代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java项目的多线程优化及其实现细节

不同观点：
• **Calzifer的观点**：Calzifer指出，在Java中，String的hashCode可能被缓存，特别是在JIT（即时编译器）优化的情况下，空循环可能被完全移除。因此，虽然代码看似在重复计算hash，但实际上可能并不会真正执行这么多次。

• **sieve的观点**：sieve讨论了书写Sanskrit术语时使用罗马字母所带来的发音问题，并建议使用IAST或ISO-15919标准来避免误读。同时，提出为了适应英文用户，某些字母如"ch"应该保留以表示其正确的发音。

• **mprataps的观点**：mprataps对收到的反馈表示感谢，并提到该项目最初是为了学习多线程技术。他表示会参考反馈进行改进，并认为项目已经达到了预期的学习目标。

• **sidcool的观点**：sidcool称赞了项目的质量，并建议添加测试以进一步提升项目。

• **sureglymop的观点**：sureglymop对多线程读取文件的效率提出质疑，认为由于系统调用和上下文切换的存在，多线程可能无法真正实现并行读取，反而会因为互相阻塞而影响性能。

• **codetiger的观点**：codetiger询问是否有与其他类似工具的基准测试对比，以评估该项目的性能和效率。

• **VWWHFSfQ的观点**：VWWHFSfQ担心项目中对内存的重复缓冲操作会导致内存占用过高，特别是在处理大批量数据时，可能存在内存性能问题。

• **gavinray的观点**：gavinray建议让操作系统处理内存分页和缓冲，而不是手动管理。他推荐使用Java的"MappedByteBuffer"或"AsynchronousFileChannel"来进行异步文件读取和处理，以提高效率。

• **ldjkfkdsjnv的观点**：ldjkfkdsjnv认为使用LLM（如GPT等）可以在几小时内写出类似的库，暗示该项目可能并不复杂或具有独特性。

• **SillyUsername的观点**：SillyUsername指出，使用ArrayList处理大量添加操作时性能不佳，建议使用LinkedList来提升吞吐量，并提到还有其他优化空间。

补充讨论：
• 项目的多线程实现细节及内存管理是讨论的核心，特别是在文件读取和处理时，多线程是否有效以及如何优化内存使用成为焦点。
• 反馈中涉及了对项目代码实现的细节优化（如数据结构的选择、内存管理）以及项目整体设计的建议（如添加测试、进行性能对比）。
• 争议焦点主要在于多线程在文件处理中的有效性及内存管理的优化策略，不同用户提出了不同的技术方案和建议。

Samchika
Samchika
(meaning
File
in Sanskrit) is a
re-usable
,
easy-to-use
, and
extremely fast
file processing library for the Java language.
It is built with a strong focus on
multithreading
to handle CPU-intensive file processing tasks in parallel, enabling high performance even with massive files.
🚀 Features
🔁 Fully multithreaded – optimized for parallel file processing.
🧩 Simple API – just plug in your file path and logic.
📊 Optional runtime stats – time taken, memory used, thread-level info.
🧪 Ideal for processing and analyzing
large text files
(e.g. logs, datasets).
🌍 Open-source friendly – contributions are welcome!
Use Cases
Samchika excels in several scenarios where multithreaded file processing provides significant advantages:
Log Analysis & Processing
ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) Operations
Large Text Corpus Processing
Batch Report Generation
Data Transformation Pipelines
Real-time Data Processing
See the examples directory for detailed implementations of these use cases.
Quick Example
java// Transform a large CSV file with optimal performance
SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("large_dataset.csv")
.outputPath("transformed_dataset.csv")
.batchSize(10000)
.lineProcessor(line -> line.toUpperCase())
.displayStats(true)
.build()
.execute();
📦 Installation
Maven
<repositories>
<repository>
<id>jitpack.io</id>
<url>https://jitpack.io</url>
</repository>
</repositories>
<dependencies>
<dependency>
<groupId>com.github.mayankpratap</groupId>
<artifactId>samchika</artifactId>
<version>1.0.0</version>
</dependency>
</dependencies>
Gradle
repositories {
maven { url 'https://jitpack.io' }
}
dependencies {
implementation 'com.github.mayankpratap:samchika:1.0.0'
}
🛠️ How to Use
Step 1: Import the Library
import com.samchika.SmartFileProcessor;
Step 2: Client Code
public static void main(String[] args) {
SmartFileProcessor processor = SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("input.txt")         // Path to the file to be processed
.outputPath("output.txt")       // Path to write the output
.lineProcessor(Main::processLine) // Your business logic per line
.displayStats(true)             // Optional: display runtime stats
.build();
processor.execute();
}
📈 Performance
Benchmarked against naïve BufferedReader-based implementations on files of various sizes:
✅ 200 MB
✅ 1 GB
✅ 5 GB
✅ 16 GB
Significant performance improvements were observed, especially in multi-core systems ( More than 70% performance gain )
The gain in time saved improves in comparison to naive code, as we increase the size of input file.  Also for huge performance gain in time, the memory used for even large files ( 16GB ) is manageable ( ~ 800 MB ).

data.author: danielam

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Alasdair MacIntyre及其作品的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [qhiliq] 认为MacIntyre的《Hegel on Faces and Skulls》对他影响很大，帮助他理解了黑格尔对面相学和颅相学的批判，并从中思考现代面部识别系统的问题。该评论关注的是从外表获取信息的局限性，并将MacIntyre的思想与技术问题联系起来。
  
• [AquinasCoder] 推荐了MacIntyre的其他作品，如《Whose Justice, Whose Rationality》和《Dependent Rational Animals》。虽然AquinasCoder认为MacIntyre在现代认识论与奥古斯丁-托马斯主义之间的调和尝试未必完全成功，但肯定了MacIntyre作为道德哲学家的地位。

• [sisoes] 提到《After Virtue》深刻改变了他的道德世界观，并对此表示感激，尽管他已经不再是罗马天主教徒。这表明MacIntyre的思想对个体道德观念有深远影响。

• [Boogie_Man] 将《After Virtue》与G.K. Chesterton的思想联系起来，表示对MacIntyre的欣赏，尤其是对他批判和分析异端思想的兴趣。

• [digiconfucius] 同样高度评价《After Virtue》，认为这本书帮助他了解了思想史，并对MacIntyre的去世表示遗憾，表达了一种未能与其见面的遗憾。

• [antithesizer] 对MacIntyre的《After Virtue》持批评态度，认为其强调道德仅存在于文化传统中的观点会导致道德相对主义，忽视了历史上许多传统社会存在的恶劣行为（如奴隶制、厌女症等）。antithesizer认为现代伦理虽然碎片化，但不能通过回归部落主义或否认理性来解决。

• [gjm11] 对MacIntyre曾将某作品描述为“哲学界的《Vogue》”表示好奇，显示出对MacIntyre某些具体观点或评价的兴趣，但未深入讨论其思想。

• [cess11] 尽管在神学和政治哲学上不同意MacIntyre的许多观点，但仍尊重他尝试与尼采及法国哲学家对话，并坚持其平等主义的伦理观。此外，cess11引用MacIntyre的一句话来展示其持续的激进立场。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：《After Virtue》中的道德相对主义倾向及其对传统文化与现代伦理关系的处理方式。antithesizer认为MacIntyre过度美化古代社区和传统，而忽视了其中存在的恶劣行为。
• 对MacIntyre思想的个人解读与情感反应，如sisoes和digiconfucius对其作品的深刻个人体验。
• MacIntyre在道德哲学和神学领域的地位与影响，多位评论者对其思想贡献表示肯定，即便在不同意其具体观点的情况下。

data.title: The Curious Case of the Pygmy Nuthatch
data.author: prawn
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在疫情期间逐渐对观鸟产生痴迷，并将其变成一种无时无刻都在进行的活动，即“birding”。观鸟不仅是观察鸟类，更是融入一种新的现实层次，解读周围环境。这种活动通常平和且有助于减压，但偶尔也会遇到意外，如电影中错误使用的鸟叫声，令观鸟爱好者感到困惑和困扰。作者特别提到在电影《查理的天使》中一个长期存在的鸟类错误，并深入调查其背后的原因，最终发现即便是高预算的大片也会在 portray 鸟类时出错。文章改编自Slate播客《Decoder Ring》的一集。

44050465.article_content:
Photo illustration by Slate. Photos by Kevin Winter/Getty Images, Bjørn Christian Tørrissen/https://bjornfree.com, and Columbia Pictures.
Tweet
Share
Share
Comment
There is nothing quite like becoming birdpilled. I am not a halfway kind of person: When I got into movies, I turned thinking about movies into my job. When I got into running, it wasn’t long until I was running a half-marathon every weekend. So I know what it’s like to become obsessed—and to start seeing your new obsession everywhere.
But during lockdown, I, like a lot of people, gradually became obsessed with birds—and it turns out that, with birds, they really are everywhere. They’re fluttering outside your window when you’re supposed to be working. They’re singing nearby when you’re supposed to be sleeping. They’re soaring overhead when you’re supposed to be paying attention to oncoming traffic.
Bird-watching does sometimes involve just that—watching birds—but for the truly birdpilled, it’s about tuning in to a new layer of reality around you and decoding it. The word
bird
becomes not just a noun but a verb, and you are
always
birding. That bird singing when you’re trying to sleep in, that sounds like a dial-up modem? That’s a song sparrow. That bird fluttering outside your window when you’re supposed to be working?
Damn
, you think,
is that a
yellow-rumped warbler
?
That raptor soaring over your head when you’re supposed to be paying attention to oncoming traffic? Usually it’s a red-tailed hawk, but sometimes it’s a turkey vulture, or a black vulture, or something more interesting, something that maybe merits glancing up just a
little
while longer …
This is your new reality, and after a few months or years of adjusting to the shock of it, you start to feel as if you’re in the Matrix. In every glimpse of an outer tail feather, every snippet of song, you can see those cascading green lines of code, and after a while, you can read them.
Most of the time, this is a peaceful, meditative activity, the kind that puts you in a flow state and has been
scientifically
proven
to
reduce stress
. No matter how out of control everything else feels, when you’re out in nature, everything is in its right place.
Still, every once in a while, there’s a glitch in the Matrix. In real life, these oddities are thrilling: If something is out of place, it could be a “vagrant,” a migrating bird that has wandered off course from another side of the country or even another hemisphere.
Advertisement
There are, unfortunately, other types of glitches. They come fast and furious, scrambling your brain. You’re watching Indiana Jones trudge through the jungles of South America in the opening scene of
Raiders of the Lost Ark
, and
one of the first sounds you hear
is the famous “
awebo
” call of the tundra-loving willow ptarmigan, on the wrong end of the American continent. You’re watching Season 3 of
The White Lotus
, set in Thailand, and you find yourself distracted by
the persistent “kon-ka-
reeee
” of red-winged blackbirds
, on the wrong side of the Pacific Ocean. You’re lost in
Dune
’s sweeping vistas, watching Paul Atreides sulk about his home planet of Caladan, until there it is, on the wrong side of the galaxy: a
killdeer
.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Like any generous viewer—I consider myself one—you learn to suspend your disbelief. The same way you learn to accept that every phone number in every movie starts with
555
, if you’re a birder, you learn to accept that every bald eagle in every movie screeches like a red-tailed hawk.
Advertisement
I maintained this policy throughout my early birdpilling. But then I watched the original movie adaptation of
Charlie’s Angels
, and I found myself staring down one of the greatest mysteries of recent cinema.
You see, there’s a scene in that movie that tormented me, that kept me up at night, and that lately has had me interrogating a wide variety of seemingly devoted, and certainly well-compensated, filmmaking professionals. That’s because the bird in
Charlie’s Angels
is, I believe, the wrongest bird in the history of cinema—and one of the weirdest and most inexplicable flubs in any movie I can remember. It is elaborately, even
ornately
wrong. It has haunted not just me but, as I’d later learn, the birding community at large for almost a quarter of a century.
So, naturally, being an all-in sort of person, I embarked upon a wild-goose chase to investigate how and why this monstrosity took flight. I talked to script doctors and scoured legal statutes. I interviewed leading ornithological experts and electronically analyzed birdcalls, all to figure out who laid this giant egg. It took nearly a year. But eventually, I discovered why hundreds of people with a budget of nearly $100 million failed to accurately portray a single bird. The answer was most fowl.
Advertisement
This story was adapted from an episode of Slate’s podcast
Decoder Ring
.
That episode was written by Forrest Wickman and edited by Willa Paskin and Evan

data.title: Caesar's Last Breath
data.author: charliesabino
data.article_summary: 《凯撒的最后一口气》一文通过费米估算的方法，估算了我们每次呼吸中吸入凯撒最后一口气中的分子数量。文章假设凯撒最后一口气的分子均匀扩散到大气中，并利用一些简化数据进行计算。结果显示，我们每次呼吸大约会吸入一个来自凯撒最后一口气的分子。文章详细列出了大气体积、一次呼吸的体积等计算步骤，并通过近似值和数量级验证了估算的合理性。这种估算方法展示了“餐巾纸数学”的强大，帮助我们理解复杂问题中的数量关系。
data.comments_summary:

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于分子是否能在2000年后仍然存在并均匀分布，以及估算模型中假设的合理性。

data.title: Bits with Soul
data.author: mrkeen
data.article_summary: 在达尔文学院的访谈中，计算机科学家Simon Peyton Jones分享了他对编程语言研究的见解。他讨论了函数式编程的重要性，特别是Haskell语言的发展。Simon强调了理论与实践结合的必要性，指出学术研究应关注实际问题。他还谈到了教育和开源社区对编程语言创新的推动作用，鼓励更多人参与其中。Simon以其在并行计算和编译器设计方面的贡献而闻名，他的观点为计算机科学领域提供了深刻的启示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学及其教育的重要性，以及如何传达其魅力与影响

不同观点：
• [flir的观点] 计算机科学不仅仅关乎编码和技术，它提供了一种新的视角来理解和探索世界。flir强调，通过数字化技术，我们能够机械化分析和转换信息，探索手动技术无法触及的领域。他指出，计算机科学具有复杂性和创造性，并且已经深入到我们的日常生活中，因此每个人，尤其是儿童，都应该对其有基本的理解和感知。他认为这不仅关乎技术能力，还涉及到理解技术的潜力和局限。

• [cpt_hellsmug的观点] cpt_hellsmug并没有直接讨论计算机科学本身，而是对flir的表达方式做出了反馈。他认为flir的演讲风格专业且客观，让人容易相信其内容，但他个人希望在其中加入更多的情感元素，使演讲更具幽默感和共鸣。他还提到自己创作了一部与此相关的漫画，尽管可能有些偏离主题。

补充讨论：
• flir强调计算机科学的创造性和美学价值，试图打破人们对计算机科学“枯燥”和“技术化”的刻板印象，呼吁教育中应包含更多对技术的感性理解。
• cpt_hellsmug则更关注表达的形式，希望在讨论严肃主题时能增加情感和幽默，使讨论更具吸引力。
• 争议的焦点可能在于如何在技术性演讲中平衡专业性和趣味性，使听众既能获取知识，又能享受过程。

总结来看，讨论的焦点在于计算机科学的教育和传播方式，以及如何在传达信息时兼顾理性和感性。

data.title: Sugar-Coated Poison: Benign Generation Unlocks LLM Jailbreaking
data.author: favoboa
data.article_summary: 这篇文章揭示了大语言模型（LLM）中存在的一种漏洞，称为防御阈值衰减（DTD）。随着模型生成大量良性内容，其注意力权重会从输入转向先前输出，从而更容易受到越狱攻击。文章提出了一种名为“糖衣毒药（SCP）”的攻击方法，通过良性输入和对抗性推理诱导模型生成恶意内容。为减轻此类攻击，文章引入了一种简单有效的防御策略POSD，显著降低越狱成功率的同时保持模型的泛化能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI jail-breaking 的可行性、RLHF（基于人类反馈的强化学习）的有效性以及相关技术文档的完整性。

不同观点：
• [waltbosz] 认为 AI jail-breaking 是一种有趣的心智锻炼。他通过合理化理由，例如为了练习应对负面自我对话，成功让AI生成了违反其原则的仇恨言论。这表明，通过巧妙的输入，可以绕过AI的安全机制。

• [umvi] 对完美的、牢不可破的LLM（大型语言模型）持保留态度，认为“安全”的定义是主观的，特别是在不同政治背景下（如中国），这种定义可能带有政治色彩。这意味着对AI安全机制的设定需要考虑文化和政治背景。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Sugar-Coated Poison: Benign Generation Unlocks LLM Jailbreaking, by Yu-Hang Wu and Yu-Jie Xiong and Jie-Zhang
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become increasingly integral to a wide range of applications. However, they still remain the threat of jailbreak attacks, where attackers manipulate designed prompts to make the models elicit malicious outputs. Analyzing jailbreak methods can help us delve into the weakness of LLMs and improve it. In this paper, We reveal a vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), which we term Defense Threshold Decay (DTD), by analyzing the attention weights of the model's output on input and subsequent output on prior output: as the model generates substantial benign content, its attention weights shift from the input to prior output, making it more susceptible to jailbreak attacks. To demonstrate the exploitability of DTD, we propose a novel jailbreak attack method, Sugar-Coated Poison (SCP), which induces the model to generate substantial benign content through benign input and adversarial reasoning, subsequently producing malicious content. To mitigate such attacks, we introduce a simple yet effective defense strategy, POSD, which significantly reduces jailbreak success rates while preserving the model's generalization capabilities.

data.title: How I ended up flying for Yemen's national airline – and survived
data.author: techonup
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在也门航空（Yemenia）工作的外籍合同工的详细情况。作者描述了一个典型外籍飞行员在航空职业生涯中可能做出的选择，因之前合同突然终止而面临失业和经济压力。在偶然机会下，他获得了一份也门航空的6个月外籍合同，包含高薪、住宿、签约奖金和其他福利。尽管有些警示信号，如面试过程简单、沟通不专业等，他仍决定参与。经过简单的线上面试和开罗的评估（旅途经济舱、住宿豪华），他通过了形式上的模拟机测试，但未签署正式合同。几周后，他被通知去开罗进行培训，并被要求提供大量个人信息。培训即将开始时，他回忆起也门航空曾发生的致命空难，暗示对未来工作的潜在担忧。
data.comments_summary:

Yemenia Expat Contract: Full Info
A carrier which is very rarely mentioned on here, Im going to give you an insight into what it is like to work for them under one of those famous expat contracts that have floated about here and there in the past. I understand 99% of you will see the advert and simply move on, perhaps with an amused exhale while you scroll down to the flag carrier DEC jobs, but for the 1% of you looking for answers, here you go!
Ill start from the beginning:
Background
:
So, you made some silly choices in your aviation career, and have found yourself fallen into the contractor bubble, jumping between contracts with various contractors. You dont see your family as often as youd like, and its far from stable, but the money is great and there is a large variety of flying.
Your previous contract blew up after just a few weeks and you find yourself now unemployed, bills to pay and a family to look after, when by miracle, a contractor rolls across your path offering a starting-6 month contracting role with Yemenia, LHS of the 320, a high roller 6 figure salary, accommodation, a joining bonus, and all the addons one might expect from this sort of contract. You know that when things seem too good to be true, they usually are, but hindsight is always 20/20, and you reassure yourself at the time that it is a reputable contractor, so dont think twice about it.
Application
:
You throw in a fairly straightforward application, not really expecting to hear back. As with all of these types of contracts, they often die out before they start, and the ones that do get up and running with high salaries are often competitive, so you dont expect to hear anything back. A few weeks pass, and youre invited to a few unsociably timed zoom interviews which take place with cameras off and audio that sounds like a 2007 era Call of Duty microphone. The interview process was inexplicably easy, with questions more evolving toward when can you start than anything more bus or career specific. Red flags, but its all good, youve crossed these bridges before when you joined other random carriers in the past and they turned out OK. Eventually they contact you and send you flight details for a trip to Cairo to complete an assessment, no say in the dates, theyve already made the bookings. Your journey to Cairo involves 2 stops via Frankfurt and Istanbul on an Economy Basic ticket, not exactly an Emirates Suite, but you are grateful that they pick up the tab. They whisk you into the Sofitel Cairo with a blank cheque to drown your sorrows, and where you can socialize with the other 7 expats here for the job, 2 Americans, a Brit, and a handful of continental Europeans, a few faces youve seen before too which is always reassuring.
The sim follows the usual rigmarole, and everybody passes with flying colours, in part due to the Egyption assessor not paying attention for 90% of it. A tick in the box, a shake of the hand and youre sent packing back to Europe with nothing but a verbal promise of being contacted. A few weeks pass by, and eventually you are contacted once again, this time offering you a training start date in just a matter of days, once again taking place in Cairo. Alongside this wonderful news, they will essentially ask you to share a generations worth of info with them, from your stamped logbook pages, to bank statements. Odd, but what do you know. Still no word on signing a contract though, so you hope that will be completed in training, and head on your merry way.
Training
:
You kiss the wife and kids goodbye and tell them youll see them when youre back from Yemen in 6 months time. Painful, but itll be worth it when you come back with pockets full of cash eh?
Not best pleased, at least the better half knows youll not get up to any funny business in that part of the world.
So you arrive in Cairo, alongside the other 7 expats who managed to navigate the gruelling selection process and sim assessment, and tuck into a few weeks of training.
Now, you are reminded of the fatal Yemenia Flight 626 crash

data.title: Now you can watch the Internet Archive preserve documents in real time
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 《Internet Archive》推出YouTube实时直播，展示微缩胶片（microfiche）的数字化过程。微缩胶片是一种存储多份缩微文档的胶片，常用于保存报纸、法庭文件和政府记录等。直播中，观众可以看到高分辨率相机拍摄胶片，并通过软件拼接图像，最终处理成可文本搜索的数字化文档并上传至公共收藏。该直播每周一至周五运行，不仅展示文档扫描过程，还播放无声电影和NASA历史图片等内容。
data.comments_summary:
根据提供的链接，以下是对该视频评论区的分析总结：

主要讨论点：视频内容的价值和意义

不同观点：
• 正面评价：许多观众认为视频内容具有启发性和教育意义，尤其是对于那些想了解未来科技和创新的人。他们提到视频很好地展示了未来技术的潜力和应用场景。

• 负面评价：部分观众认为视频内容过于理想化，缺乏现实依据。他们指出视频中的一些技术在实际应用中可能会遇到很多困难和挑战，比如基础设施建设和高昂的成本。

Now you can watch the Internet Archive preserve documents in real time
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
by
Emma Roth
May 22, 2025, 4:10 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Screenshot: The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
If you’ve ever wondered how the Internet Archive uploads all the physical documents on its site, now you can get a behind-the-scenes look at the process.
The Internet Archive launched
a new
YouTube livestream
that shows the digitization of microfiche in real time — complete with some relaxing, lo-fi beats.
Microfiche is a sheet of film that contains multiple images of miniaturized documents. It’s an old form of storing newspapers, court documents, government records, and other important documents. The Internet Archive uses these microfiche cards to digitize and upload documents to its online library.
The livestream shows a close-up look at one of the five microfiche digitization stations at the organization’s Richmond, California location, along with a look at the document that it’s working on. App maker Sophia Tung, who
created a LoFi music livestream showing
Waymo’s robotaxis returning to their parking lot, also
set up the microfiche livestream for the Internet Archive
.
“Operators feed microfiche cards beneath a high-resolution camera, which captures multiple detailed images of each sheet,” Chris Freeland, the Internet Archive’s director of library services, writes in a post on the site. “Software stitches these images together, after which other team members use automated tools to identify and crop up to 100 individual pages per card.”
From there, the Internet Archive processes the pages, makes them text-searchable, and then uploads them to its public collections.
The livestream runs from Monday through Friday from 10:30AM ET to 6:30PM ET. “During the day, you’ll see scanners working on custom machines to digitize all the microfiche in the world,” Tung says. “During the off hours, you can also see everything else that the Archive has to offer, like silent films in the public domain or historical pictures from NASA.”

data.title: Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在GNU Compiler Collection 15中实现的 prime path coverage 支持，这是一种通过程序执行路径进行结构化覆盖率测试的指标。该方法在测试数量和覆盖率之间取得平衡，要求循环被执行多次或跳过。研究表明，prime path coverage 涵盖了修改条件/决策覆盖（MC/DC）。通过使用后缀树修剪重复子路径，算法效率从 $O(n^2m^2)$ 提升至 $O(n^2m)$。该方法通过控制流图分析，以语言无关的方式观察和检测路径，并准确报告实现覆盖所需的代码执行顺序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：循环的退出条件是否必须被执行/不执行

不同观点：
• nullc的观点：nullc提到在处理带有"if(foo)break;"这种逻辑的循环时，经常发现bug，质疑是否所有退出条件都需要明确被执行或不执行。这暗示了对循环退出条件处理的潜在问题和复杂性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论焦点：争议的焦点在于循环中的"if(foo)break;"逻辑是否会导致不可预见的问题，特别是在退出条件没有被明确控制的情况下。这可能涉及到代码的可读性、可维护性以及潜在的错误风险。
• 例子：nullc以自己遇到的多起相关bug为例，说明这种模式可能在实际编码中引发问题，但未给出具体bug细节或场景。

总结：讨论围绕循环退出条件的处理，特别是使用"if(foo)break;"逻辑时可能引发的潜在问题。nullc基于自身经验提出了对这种写法的质疑，但没有深入展开技术细节。

Computer Science > Programming Languages
arXiv:2505.14694
(cs)
[Submitted on 25 Apr 2025]
Title:
Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection
Authors:
Jørgen Kvalsvik
View a PDF of the paper titled Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection, by J{\o}rgen Kvalsvik
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We describe the implementation of the prime path coverage support introduced the GNU Compiler Collection 15, a structural coverage metric that focuses on paths of execution through the program. Prime path coverage strikes a good balance between the number of tests and coverage, and requires that loops are taken, taken more than once, and skipped. We show that prime path coverage subsumes modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC). We improve on the current state-of-the-art algorithms for enumerating prime paths by using a suffix tree for efficient pruning of duplicated and redundant subpaths, reducing it to $O(n^2m)$ from $O(n^2m^2)$, where $n$ is the length of the longest path and $m$ is the number of candidate paths. We can efficiently track candidate paths using a few bitwise operations based on a compact representation of the indices of the ordered prime paths. By analyzing the control flow graph, GCC can observe and instrument paths in a language-agnostic manner, and accurately report what code must be run in what order to achieve coverage.

data.title: Realtek's $10 tiny 10GbE NIC will hit motherboards soon
data.author: Tuldok
data.article_summary: Realtek即将推出价格低廉的RTL8127 10GbE网络控制器，尺寸为9mm x 9mm，支持2.5 Gbps、5 Gbps和10 Gbps以太网速度，功耗约1.95W，并具备硬件级误差校正和循环冗余校验等功能，适用于主板、笔记本电脑和各种设备。该控制器预计今年晚些时候以约10美元的价格出售，可能推动10GbE在主流PC中的普及。然而，10GbE网络的普及还面临基础设施成本较高的挑战，如支持10GbE的交换机和电缆价格较贵。主板厂商可能从2025年底开始将10GbE作为高端产品的 premium 功能推出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：10GbE网络模块及其在消费级市场和企业级市场中的应用和选择

不同观点：
• WarOnPrivacy认为新的网络模块在能耗和发热方面优于现有的10GbE选项，并提到Intel I225芯片在2022-2024年间存在很多问题，而Realtek表现相对稳定，可能是一个更好的选择。他还表示对Intel 225/226的改进抱有期待。

• PaulKeeble指出消费级市场需要一种紧凑的光纤连接方案，而不是sfp+，因为后者不适合安装在典型家用主板上。他认为虽然铜缆在10Gb传输中还能应付，但转向光纤是不可避免的趋势，而企业级解决方案并不适合家用市场。

• diggan提到AQC107芯片价格昂贵，不适合主板集成，并质疑10GbE主板的成本是否合理。他分享了自己购买相关设备的经历，并怀疑主板厂商可能通过集成10GbE NIC来提高售价。

• ReverseCold对文章内容表示困惑，指出高端PC主板已经配备10GbE端口多年，并质疑文章中所提的新方案是否更便宜。他还提供了pcpartpicker上的相关主板列表作为参考。

• misja111关注连接10Gb交换机/路由器所需的电缆类型，询问是否必须使用玻璃纤维。

• q3k强烈建议使用常规的SFP+，表现出对其他方案的不满。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了10GbE在消费级和企业级市场中的不同需求和解决方案。
• 讨论了不同芯片和网络接口在性能、价格和集成度方面的优劣，如Intel、Realtek和AQC107。
• 对光纤和铜缆在10Gb传输中的适用性进行了探讨。
• 争议焦点在于10GbE解决方案的性价比及其在消费级市场中的适用性。

44071701.article_content:
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Recent updates
Update: 07:30 am (ET) 5/23
: Realtek itself has demonstrated its RTL8127 NIC working with an unknown switch using cheap CAT5E cables, and the company’s representatives at the booth emphasised this fact. However, we do not know which switch or router the company used. Yet, most 10GbE routers and switches are designed for CAT6 cabling.
Although there are many higher-end motherboards that feature 2.5GbE or even 5GbE network ports, only some of them feature a 10GbE network adapter due to cost concerns. However, this may change later this year as Realtek is prepping an inexpensive 10GbE controller that is aimed at motherboards. The controller is being showcased at
Computex 2025
.
The Realtek RTL8127 is a tiny — measuring 9mm x 9mm — network controller with a PCIe 4.0 x2 interface that supports a wide range of Ethernet speeds, including 2.5 Gbps, 5 Gbps, and 10 Gbps. The RTL8127 controller consumes about 1.95W and supports modern standby modes, which is critical for laptops. The controller integrates hardware-level error correction (ECC) and cyclic redundancy check (CRC) features to ensure reliable connections and data integrity during transmission. Also, the unit features built-in self-loopback diagnostic functions for easier maintenance.
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
The 10GBase-T technology has been used primarily in servers and high-end workstations, but its adoption for more mainstream PCs has been slow, to put it mildly. Aquantia tried to popularize it for enthusiasts in the late 2010s, then it got acquired by Marvell in 2019, and while the company still sells the AQC107 silicon, it is quite expensive for motherboard integration, and add-on cards are, by definitio,n more expensive than integrated solutions.

Features of the RTL8127 make it ideal for a range of applications, including integration into motherboards, laptops, add-on Ethernet cards, and various customer premises equipment (CPE). Perhaps more importantly, Realtek plans to sell these chips for about $10 starting later this year, which will make its integration a much more appealing endeavor for motherboard makers.
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Of course, producers of mainboards will sell the 10GbE as a premium feature starting from late 2025 – early 2026, so expect 10GbE connectivity to be a part of higher-end offerings and to that end we can only wonder how much will desktop motherboards with a 10GbE cost.
Of course, just like earlier, the big concern is how much the infrastructure (switches, access points, etc.) supporting 10GbE costs. At present, the cheapest 10GBase-T switch from TP-Link costs
$299 at Newegg,
and, of course, this switch requires CAT6 or CAT6A cables, which are also not cheap, making a 10GbE network a pretty expensive endeavor. Then again, if there are a lot of motherboards with a cheap 10GbE NIC, demand for switches goes up, and they will get cheaper. However, we can only wonder when this time comes.

44071701.article_summary: Realtek即将推出价格低廉的RTL8127 10GbE网络控制器，尺寸为9mm x 9mm，支持2.5 Gbps、5 Gbps和10 Gbps以太网速度，功耗约1.95W，并具备硬件级误差校正和循环冗余校验等功能，适用于主板、笔记本电脑和各种设备。该控制器预计今年晚些时候以约10美元的价格出售，可能推动10GbE在主流PC中的普及。然而，10GbE网络的普及还面临基础设施成本较高的挑战，如支持10GbE的交换机和电缆价格较贵。主板厂商可能从2025年底开始将10GbE作为高端产品的 premium 功能推出。

data.article_summary: 文章描绘了2030年一个早晨的routine，充满了各种人工智能（AI）助手。主人公早上5:30被一个名为Kyle的AI闹钟唤醒，随后在穿衣、喝咖啡、系鞋带、出门、乘电梯等每个环节，都被不同的AI助手包围，不断推销自己的功能。在健身房，由于接待AI超出API限额，主人公直接进入更衣室，并与储物柜进行一系列复杂的认证操作。锻炼后，再次面对繁琐的登录程序。最终，坐上名为Ulysses的智能汽车去上班，再次被AI介绍其功能。文章以幽默方式展现了未来被AI充斥的生活，暗示技术过度渗透可能带来的繁琐和无奈。
