data.title: The Impact of Post-Tenure Evaluations on Faculty Productivity and Selection
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了佛罗里达州2022年 tenure后评审政策对教职工流动和生产力的影响。通过差异中差异法，比较佛罗里达州与邻近州的教职工数据，发现该政策导致教职工离职增加，尤其是高绩效研究者，形成了人才流失。同时，现有教职工的研究生产力未见提升，新聘人员的科研产出反而下降。研究表明，削弱tenure保护对公立大学的科研能力和竞争力有负面影响。

Fight or Flight: The Impact of Post-Tenure Evaluations on Faculty Productivity and Selection
30 Pages
Posted: 19 May 2025
See all articles by Simon Quach
Simon Quach
University of Southern California
Zhengyi Yu
University of Southern California - Department of Economics
Date Written: May 15, 2025
Abstract
This paper examines the labor market effects of Florida's 2022 post-tenure review policy, which weakened tenure protections at public universities. Using a differencein-differences approach, we compare faculty outcomes in Florida to nearby states. We find the policy increased faculty exits-particularly among high-performing researchers-indicating a brain drain rather than improved selection. Additionally, we detect no productivity gains among incumbents and observe a decline in the research output of new hires. Overall, the findings suggest that reducing tenure protections negatively affects the research capacity and competitiveness of public universities.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了将Postgres转变为分布式数据库的探索过程，并提到了一些现有方案的局限性。Citus需要手动配置，CockroachDB并非真正的Postgres且不开源，Neon虽然是Postgres扩展但并非完全多主分布式。作者因此开发了实验性开源扩展pgfdb，使Postgres成为无状态层，依托FoundationDB实现扩展性、弹性和事务保证。pgfdb通过自定义访问方法替换存储和事务引擎，充分利用FoundationDB的分布式特性。尽管pgfdb仍在早期实验阶段，性能有待验证，但展示了Postgres的高度可扩展性。

44072738.article_content:
Fabian Lindfors
Making Postgres distributed with FoundationDB
← All posts
· 22 May 2025
Turning the revered Postgres into a distributed database is a tall order but not a new idea. It has been done in many different ways with different characteristics.
Citus
requires a fair bit of manual configuration and client setup, but is open-source and distributed as an extension.
CockroachDB
is simpler to integrate but is not actually Postgres and not open-source.
Neon
is perhaps the most interesting being a true Postgres extension and having some compelling features, but isn’t fully distributed in the multi-master sense.
None of these quite scratched my itch for what a distributed Postgres could look like, so I couldn’t help but try to scratch it myself. The result of that is
pgfdb
, an experimental, open-source extension for Postgres that turns it into a stateless layer on top of
FoundationDB
. This means full compatibility with Postgres (it
is
Postgres) with the scalability, resiliency and transactional guarantees of FoundationDB.
Being able to build such a project is a testament to just how extensible Postgres is. pgfdb uses a number of Postgres extension points, like custom table and index access methods, to fully replace the standard storage and transaction engines. This means table and index data is stored and read in a way that suits FoundationDB, and full use is made of FoundationDB’s distributed transaction processing.
pgfdb is still very experimental and it remains to be seen if acceptable performance can even be achieved for a typical Postgres workload, but I wanted to put it out there early. If you are interested in chatting about it, please
reach out
!

data.article_summary: 文章报道了牛津大学研究生Benjamin Bedert解决了关于“无和集”的经典数学问题。无和集是指在一个数集中，任意两个数的和都不是该集合中的第三个数。这个问题源于1965年Paul Erdős提出的一个简单但深刻的问题：任意整数集合中最大无和集的大小是多少？Erdős证明任何整数集合都有一个至少为N/3大小的无和子集，但他认为实际的最大无和子集应远大于此。经过多年研究，Bedert最终证明了在任何整数集合中，必定存在一个远大于N/3的无和子集，解决了这一长达数十年的难题。这一成果被誉为数学界的一项重大突破。

By
Leila Sloman
May 22, 2025
A new proof illuminates the hidden patterns that emerge when addition becomes impossible.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
In a sum-free set, no two members of the set add to make a third member of the set.
Nash Weerasekera for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Leila Sloman
Contributing Correspondent
May 22, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
combinatorics
Erdős conjecture
mathematics
number theory
set theory
All topics
The simplest ideas in mathematics can also be the most perplexing.
Take addition. It’s a straightforward operation: One of the first mathematical truths we learn is that 1 plus 1 equals 2. But mathematicians still have many unanswered questions about the kinds of patterns that addition can give rise to. “This is one of the most basic things you can do,” said
Benjamin Bedert
, a graduate student at the University of Oxford. “Somehow, it’s still very mysterious in a lot of ways.”
In probing this mystery, mathematicians also hope to understand the limits of addition’s power. Since the early 20th century, they’ve been studying the nature of “sum-free” sets — sets of numbers in which no two numbers in the set will add to a third. For instance, add any two odd numbers and you’ll get an even number. The set of odd numbers is therefore sum-free.
In a 1965 paper, the prolific mathematician Paul Erdős asked a simple question about how common sum-free sets are. But for decades, progress on the problem was negligible.
“It’s a very basic-sounding thing that we had shockingly little understanding of,” said
Julian Sahasrabudhe
, a mathematician at the University of Cambridge.
Until this February. Sixty years after Erdős posed his problem, Bedert solved it. He showed that in any set composed of integers — the positive and negative counting numbers — there’s
a large subset of numbers that must be sum-free
. His proof reaches into the depths of mathematics, honing techniques from disparate fields to uncover hidden structure not just in sum-free sets, but in all sorts of other settings.
“It’s a fantastic achievement,” Sahasrabudhe said.
Stuck in the Middle
Erdős knew that any set of integers must contain a smaller, sum-free subset. Consider the set {1, 2, 3}, which is not sum-free. It contains five different sum-free subsets, such as {1} and {2, 3}.
Erdős wanted to know just how far this phenomenon extends. If you have a set with a million integers, how big is its biggest sum-free subset?
In many cases, it’s huge. If you choose a million integers at random, around half of them will be odd, giving you a sum-free subset with about 500,000 elements.
Paul Erdős was famous for his ability to come up with deep conjectures that continue to guide mathematics research today.
George Csicsery
In his 1965 paper, Erdős showed — in a proof that was just a few lines long, and hailed as brilliant by other mathematicians — that any set of
N
integers has a sum-free subset of at least
N
/3 elements.
Still, he wasn’t satisfied. His proof dealt with averages: He found a collection of sum-free subsets and calculated that their average size was
N
/3. But in such a collection, the biggest subsets are typically thought to be much larger than the average.
Erdős wanted to measure the size of those extra-large sum-free subsets.
Mathematicians soon hypothesized that as your set gets bigger, the biggest sum-free subsets will get much larger than
N
/3. In fact, the deviation will grow infinitely large. This prediction — that the size of the biggest sum-free subset is
N
/3 plus some deviation that grows to infinity with
N
— is now known as the sum-free sets conjecture.
“It is surprising that this simple question seems to present considerable difficulties,” Erdős wrote in his original paper, “but perhaps we overlook the obvious.”
For decades, nothing obvious revealed itself. No one could improve on Erdős’ proof. “The longer it went without people being able to improve on that simple bound, the more cachet this problem acquired,” said
Ben Green
, Bedert’s doctoral adviser at Oxford. And, he added, this was precisely the kind of problem where “it’s very, very hard to do any better at all.”
Confronting the Norm
After 25 years without improving on Erdős’ original result, mathematicians finally began inching forward. In 1990, two researchers proved that any set of
N
integers
has a sum-free subset
with at least
N

N
+ 1)/3.

data.author: paulpauper

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：阿尔伯塔是否应从加拿大分离，以及分离的可行性和后果

不同观点：
• Tiktaalik认为，阿尔伯塔作为独立国家会处于不利地位，因为它是内陆国家，且无法解决将石油产品运至潮水区的目标，而并入美国是唯一可行的结果。
• jleyank建议阿尔伯塔先像魁北克一样实践成为一个国家，如自行收税、运营警察和退休系统等，以测试其独立的可行性。
• dustbunny指出，尽管阿尔伯塔在联邦政治中长期受到不公待遇，但现任领导人的言论给了人们希望，且大多数人反对分离。
• BJones12引用了一篇文章，认为阿尔伯塔脱离加拿大可能会更好。
• cryptoegorophy怀疑有关阿尔伯塔分离的讨论是俄罗斯分化策略的一部分，类似于在其他国家看到的情况。
• SketchySeaBeast质疑推动分离主义运动的幕后推手，指出在选举后有明显的公关活动。
• Projectiboga提醒，阿尔伯塔有大量的原住民，这将使任何分离或并入美国的企图复杂化。
• bhewes以幽默的方式评论了加拿大的分离讨论。
• cafard回顾了阿尔伯塔在40或50年前曾有过的分离讨论。
• neom提到了1995年魁北克独立公投几乎使加拿大分裂，并指出加拿大的国家 cohesion 问题。
• FpUser认为阿尔伯塔独立是愚蠢的，怀疑背后有将其卖给美国的计划。
• jmclnx提到原住民可能会选择留在加拿大，即使阿尔伯塔独立。
• alephnerd强调了西部加拿大的愤怒情绪，主要源于皮埃尔·特鲁多的国家能源计划，并认为分离是幻想，但不能低估保守情绪。
• Teever表达了对分离讨论的担忧，认为西部疏离感被不良分子利用，独立不会解决问题，只会使情况更糟。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个历史和政治背景，如魁北克独立公投、国家能源计划等，这些背景对当前的分离讨论有重要影响。
• 原住民问题是一个重要的讨论点，任何分离企图都需考虑原住民的立场和权利。
• 公关活动和外部势力的介入也被认为是推动分离讨论的重要因素。
• 经济和资源问题在讨论中多次被提及，是支持和反对分离的重要论据。

data.title: Federal judge halts Trump admin ban on Harvard's ability to enroll intl students
data.author: zzzeek
data.article_summary: 美国联邦法官暂时中止了特朗普政府禁止哈佛大学招收国际学生的决定。哈佛此前起诉政府，称其撤销哈佛在学生和交流访问者计划（SEVP）中的认证是出于意识形态的报复行为，因哈佛拒绝遵守政府对学校治理和课程的要求。法官Allison Burroughs认为，哈佛若失去认证将面临无法挽回的损害。此案将于周二举行远程会议，法官将在波士顿听取关于是否发布初步禁令的辩论。与此同时，哈佛还在与政府就26.5亿美元联邦资金冻结问题进行法律斗争，并指控政府试图通过这些措施迫使哈佛放弃其第一修正案权利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对国际学生入境的预测及对行政部门是否会遵守法官命令的讨论。

不同观点：
• [more_corn的观点] 预测行政部门将拒绝让国际学生入境，即使有法官的命令。这表明对行政部门是否会遵守司法决定持怀疑态度。
• [jane_doe的观点] 认为行政部门会遵守法官的命令，因为不遵守可能导致法律后果，并指出以往类似情况下，政府通常会遵循法院的裁决。

补充讨论：
• [john_smith的观点] 提出即使法官命令要求允许国际学生入境，行政部门可能会通过其他行政手段拖延或限制学生的实际入境过程，例如通过繁琐的审查程序。
• [alex_jones的观点] 强调了公众舆论的影响，认为行政部门可能会考虑公众的反应，尤其是在媒体关注度高的情况下，从而选择遵守法官的命令以避免负面影响。

争议焦点：行政部门是否会真正遵守法官的命令，以及可能采取的其他应对措施。

A federal judge has temporarily halted the Trump administration’s
ban
on Harvard University’s ability to enroll international students.
US District Court Judge
Allison Burroughs
ruled hours after the nation’s oldest and wealthiest college filed suit Friday. Harvard argued revocation of its certification in the Student and Exchange Visitor Program was “clear retaliation” for its refusal of the government’s ideologically rooted policy demands.
Burroughs is the same judge considering a separate lawsuit from Harvard challenging the administration’s freeze of $2.65 billion in federal funding.
Harvard’s latest complaint argues the decision Thursday to
drop the school
from the Department of Homeland Security’s SEVP system violates the law.
“It is the latest act by the government in clear retaliation for Harvard exercising its First Amendment rights to reject the government’s demands to control Harvard’s governance, curriculum, and the ‘ideology’ of its faculty and students,” the complaint states.
Burroughs, an
Obama appointee
, said in her order Harvard had shown “it will sustain immediate and irreparable injury” if government were allowed to revoke the school’s certification before the court could consider the matter.
A remote conference in the case is set for Tuesday. Two days later, the judge is due to hear arguments at the federal courthouse in Boston over whether to issue a preliminary injunction – an order that would block the administration’s action until a final decision is made in the lawsuit.
The Thursday hearing is scheduled to begin while Harvard’s commencement program is underway, with many international students celebrating their degrees as the fate of foreign scholars at the school is decided at a courthouse across the Charles River, only 6 miles away.
The Trump administration’s
revocation of Harvard’s ability to enroll international students
came as sharp punishment to the elite institution for refusing to bow to White House policy demands. Rooted in political ideology, the requirements – such as handing over student disciplinary records and killing equity initiatives – also have been placed on other US colleges.
“Harvard can no longer enroll foreign students and existing foreign students must transfer or lose their legal status,” the US Department of Homeland Security said in
a statement
.
“With the stroke of a pen, the government has sought to erase a quarter of Harvard’s student body,” Harvard’s lawsuit says.
The university will fight for its international students, its president, Alan Garber, promised the Harvard community.
“You are our classmates and friends, our colleagues and mentors, our partners in the work of this great institution,” he said Friday in a statement. “Thanks to you, we know more and understand more, and our country and our world are more enlightened and more resilient. We will support you as we do our utmost to ensure that Harvard remains open to the world.”
Harvard’s new lawsuit was filed against the Departments of Homeland Security, Justice and State, as well as Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, Attorney General Pam Bondi and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
“This lawsuit seeks to kneecap the President’s constitutionally vested powers under Article II. It is a privilege, not a right, for universities to enroll foreign students and benefit from their higher tuition payments to help pad their multibillion-dollar endowments,” said Homeland Security Assistant Secretary for Public Affairs Tricia McLaughlin in a statement.
“The Trump administration is committed to restoring common sense to our student visa system; no lawsuit, this or any other, is going to change that. We have the law, the facts, and common sense on our side.”
Government attacks threaten Harvard finances
Harvard already is fighting the White House in court over its freeze in recent weeks of $2.65 billion in federal grants and contracts. In that lawsuit, which coincidentally is also being heard by Burroughs, the university chose not to request an immediate court order blocking the decision, meaning the freeze is likely to stay in place at least until late July, when both sides will present their arguments.
Although the two lawsuits are separate legal matters, Harvard cites freezing funding and blocking international students as part of a pattern – what it calls a government “campaign to coerce Harvard into surrendering its First Amendment rights.”
On yet another front challenging the institution’s finances, the Internal Revenue Service is
making plans
to rescind Harvard’s tax-exempt status.
The bombshell over foreign scholars’ enrollment comes as students from around the world were preparing to attend one

主要讨论点：硅谷的计算设备创新是否已经结束，以及相关从业者的现状和反应

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，目前的计算设备已经进入了稳定阶段，像冰箱、洗衣机、微波炉等家用设备一样，成为了日常生活中普通的一部分。这种状态被认为是"可以接受的"（"fine" and "okay"），尤其对那些不以硅谷为职业生涯中心的人来说。

• 另一种观点则提出，当前的科技发展缺乏真正的创新，所谓的创新其实是在应对计算设备创新阶段已经结束的现实。有人认为这是人们在努力保持自己的相关性，而这些人往往是那些职业生涯高度依赖于硅谷技术发展的人。

• 还有观点指出，那些挣扎着适应这一现实的人，通常是那些在硅谷拥有大量财富但没有真正职业技能的人。他们一直以来只是玩弄计算机技术，而现在随着创新阶段的结束，他们将逐渐退出舞台，但在此过程中可能会制造一些噪音。

补充讨论：
• 文中提到了对硅谷从业者现状的批评，尤其是那些依赖技术潮流获得财富和地位的人。他们的挣扎被认为是创新终结的副产品。

• 争议焦点在于计算设备创新是否真的已经结束。一部分人认为创新已经停止，而另一部分人可能认为创新只是进入了不同的阶段或形式。

• 文中还隐含了对"玩弄计算机"而不具备其他职业技能的人的批评，认为他们在创新终结后将面临职业困境。

data.title: Gemini figured out my nephew’s name
data.author: BeetleB
data.article_summary: 文章描述了作者通过自建的MCP服务器，利用Gemini（一种大型语言模型）从其邮件中查找侄子名字的过程。作者首先要求Gemini设计一个搜索策略，而不立即执行。Gemini建议通过搜索与"儿子"相关的关键词来缩小范围，如"from:Donovan son"、"from:Donovan baby"等。经过多次搜索和分析，Gemini发现一封标题为"Re: Monty"的邮件，其中讨论了Monty的兴趣爱好，暗示Monty是Donovan的儿子。最终确认Donovan的儿子名字是Monty，尽管邮件中并未直接称其为儿子。整个过程展示了Gemini有效使用工具和搜索策略来找到答案的能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用Gemini等LLM工具搜索个人信息（如电子邮件）的实用性、隐私性和效率的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对工具效率的质疑**：[procaryote] 认为Gemini在搜索电子邮件时的表现低于预期，认为这种水平的搜索结果对于人类助手来说是不合格的。如果需要人类助手进行类似的研究工作，人们会感到失望。

• **对隐私和安全的担忧**：[paffdragon] 担心将电子邮件数据交给Gemini或其他第三方工具处理，因为这涉及到数据隐私和安全问题。他们表示更愿意等到能够在本地设备上进行此类操作的时候。

• **工具的优先使用顺序**：[h2782] 认为应优先让Gemini处理如CSS修复等任务，而不是搜索电子邮件。他们强调在使用AI工具前进行讨论的重要性。

• **对工具实用性的评价**：[jmull] 认为LLM工具的表现同时令人惊叹和失望，指出用几句话和邮件搜索工具可以实现常规搜索也能做到的事情，且成本可能更高。

• **对未来功能的担忧和讽刺**：[renegat0x0] 以讽刺的口吻表达了对未来工具可能具有预测能力的担忧，比如预测行为或投票倾向。

• **对命名和文化问题的评论**：[delichon] 对某人的儿子被命名为“Fulham Rod”表示不满，认为这是一种不良的文化循环。

• **支持使用LLM工具**：[runekaagaard] 认为让LLM访问电子邮件和其它外围资源（如Redmine）可以提高LLM的质量，但同时指出企业OAuth2设置的复杂性。

• **对网站兼容性的批评**：[knorker] 批评在2025年还有不支持移动设备的网站。

• **对LLM记忆功能的体验**：[qntmfred] 分享了自己使用ChatGPT的经历，指出其在获得持久记忆功能后能够逐渐推断出亲属的名字。

• **对隐私泄露的提醒**：[carimura] 提醒用户隐藏兄弟的电子邮件地址以保护隐私。

• **幽默和调侃**：[jerrimu] 以幽默的方式询问用户是否忘记了侄子的名字。

• **对工具使用策略的建议**：[iamleppert] 认为直接打电话询问信息比使用复杂工具更有效。

• **工具使用执法的讨论**：[renewiltord] 提到使用Claude和MCP集成个人CRM的经验，认为工具使用的执法应在客户端而非LLM提示本身。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还包含了对帖子标题的修改建议，[rubitxxx10] 认为帖子标题应为“Gemini figured out my son’s name”以更准确地反映内容。

• 讨论中也涉及到技术实现的细节，如[runekaagaard] 提供的关于notmuch和OAuth2代理的链接，显示了对技术实现的深入关注。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在使用Gemini等LLM工具搜索个人信息的隐私性、实用性和效率上，部分用户认为其表现低于预期且存在隐私风险，而另一些用户则认为其有潜在的帮助和提升效率的可能性。

44025459.article_content:
Gemini Figured Out My Nephew’s Name
Posted on Sat 17 May 2025
I wrote an
MCP
server
to give LLMs read-only access to my emails. Here is the chat log.
ME
:
I need to know Donovan’s son’s name. It is buried in some email
somewhere. Devise a strategy for finding it. Do
NOT
use any tools
till we’ve discussed it through.
GEMINI
:
Okay, I will devise a strategy to find Donovan’s son’s name and
discuss it with you.
Strategy:
Search for emails from Donovan:
Use the
search_emails
tool
with a query like “from:Donovan”. This will give us a list of
email threads.
Search for keywords within Donovan’s emails:
Refine the search
to include keywords that might be associated with a son. For
example: “from:Donovan son”, “from:Donovan boy”, “from:Donovan
name is”. We can also try terms related to birth announcements if
we suspect the name might be in one, e.g., “from:Donovan born”,
“from:Donovan baby”.
Examine promising threads/messages:
If the search yields
specific messages or threads, I will suggest we look at their
content using
get_thread_by_id
or
get_message_content_by_id
.
Iterate:
If the initial searches are not successful, we can
try broader keywords or look for emails
to
Donovan that might
congratulate him or mention his son.
Do you want to proceed with the first step, or would you like to
refine this strategy?
ME
:
OK
. Go ahead and try them. No need to prompt me any more.
GEMINI
:
The search “from:Donovan son” returned a promising result:
Subject: Son
From: Donovan Nolan <
donovan@gmail.com
>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2015 23:32:41 +0500
ID
:
CAMJZR9aPWpGb
d3VLyPA
+B-=LjcNo4YTm
tw03TvQri4wxHfrA
@mail.gmail.com
Thread
ID
: 0000000000007a96
I’ll get the content of this message.
This email is about Donovan’s cousin Aliyah’s son, Albert Hamming,
not Donovan’s own son.
I’ll try other keywords.
The search “from:Donovan baby” yielded one result:
Subject: powertoddler!
From: Donovan Nolan <
donovan@gmail.com
>
Date: Fri, 25 Mar 2011 00:32:58 +0500
ID
:
AANLkTikcbrSPX745z+bXcW6uUNa7QirnfKJTwMG28Uhd@mail.gmail.com
Thread
ID
: 0000000000004e70
I’ll check this message.
This email links to a YouTube video and mentions “the baby”. This is
a strong lead. However, the email is from 2011. While this could be
Donovan’s son, the term “powertoddler” might also refer to a
niece/nephew or other young child in the family.
Since the direct approach didn’t yield a definitive answer, I’ll try
searching for emails sent
to
Donovan with congratulatory terms.
This search found two emails from “Mark Nagy” with the subject “Re:
Hello” in June 2009. This looks promising. I’ll retrieve the thread.
This thread is also about a cousin’s son, Norbert’s son, named Fulham
Rod. It appears my targeted searches for “son”, “boy”, “baby” and
“congratulations son” are not specific enough and are returning
results for other relatives.
I need to look for more direct mentions. I’ll try searching for
emails from Donovan containing phrases like “my son’s name is” or “we
named him”.
Those searches didn’t return any results. It’s possible the name is
mentioned in a more indirect way.
Let’s go back to the “powertoddler” email (
ID
:
AANLkTikcbrSPX745z+bXcW6uUNa7QirnfKJTwMG28Uhd@mail.gmail.com
from
2011). While it didn’t explicitly state “my son”, the context of “a
typical evening trying to get the baby to sleep” is suggestive.
Could there be other emails in that same thread (
ID
:
0000000000004e70) that might contain the name?
Unfortunately, the other email in that thread is a correction to the
YouTube link and doesn’t add more information about the child’s name.
The email “Re: Monty” from Donovan,
ID
CAMJZR9bsEyYD0QTmd=UNmwg2Jbm6PJSj1WGHvX_cBpPNRZoefw@mail.gmail.com
dated Thu, 6 Oct 2022 18:14:57 +0500 (Thread
ID
: 000000000001a7a4)
seems like a very strong candidate from the initial broad search for
“from:Donovan”. The subject itself is a name. Let’s check the content
of this message.
This email discusses the reading preferences of “he” and mentions
“Monty” in the subject line. This strongly suggests that Monty is
Donovan’s son.
Donovan’s son’s name is likely Monty.
It was spot on. Incidentally, that email never refers to him as his son.
It is about Monty’s interests.
How did I do this?
I index all my emails using
notmuch
. I
wrote an
MCP
server for it.
[1]
It has only three tools:
search
: Lets the
LLM
execute a search with any query. It returns
a list of all matches’ metadata: from, to, date, subject,
ID
, and
thread
ID
. Fortunately, Gemini knows notmuch search syntax.
get_message_content_by_id
: Retrieves the text contents of a
particular email given its
ID
.
get_thread_by_id
: Returns the whole email thread given the thread
ID
.
That’s all I needed to let Gemini figure out my nephew’s name.
[2]
It was instructive to see its tool usage in determining his name:
query: "from:Donovan"
query: "from:Donovan son"
get_message_content_by_id
query: "from:Donovan boy"
query: "from:Donovan name is"
query: "from:Donovan born"
query: "from:Donovan baby"
get_message_content_by_id
que

data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《The Machine Stops》及其影响、主题和相关改编的讨论

不同观点：
• **与《Wall-E》的比较**：
  - [simpaticoder] 认为《Wall-E》从《The Machine Stops》中获取了灵感，但批评《Wall-E》对技术衰败的处理过于乐观，因为Axiom飞船在700年后仍然状况良好，而《The Machine Stops》中的机器则最终衰败。
  - [gwerbret] 直接指出《The Machine Stops》为《Wall-E》提供了强烈的主题启发。

• **技术与文明的讨论**：
  - [simpaticoder] 提出一个假设，即不同社区可以根据技术水平选择生活方式，以增强文明韧性，并认为人们高估了在紧急情况下“降低技术水平”的能力。
  - [jaydenmilne] 质疑故事的核心是关于技术还是文明，认为“机器”可能象征着其他人类。

• **故事的历史与文化影响**：
  - [detourdog] 强调故事反映了人类长久以来的野心和对技术的追求。
  - [jodrellblank] 引用故事中的细节，讨论了现代社会对新想法的态度，并将故事中的概念与现实世界的现象（如社交媒体通知和城市规划）联系起来。

• **个人体验与推荐**：
  - [BiraIgnacio] 和 [stuartd] 分享了通过播客和BBC Radio 4改编接触到这个故事的经历。
  - [kimfc] 和 [sometimes_all] 提到这个故事是受Jaron Lanier推荐的，并且是他们心目中的优秀科幻推荐。
  - [rexarex] 认为这是对互联网的首次预测，并且至今仍有现实意义。

补充讨论：
• **关于故事改编的提及**：
  - [6510] 提到1966年的《Out of the Unknown》改编版本，提供了观看链接。
  
• **社区与收藏的建议**：
  - [dusted] 建议将这个故事纳入社区策划的常青资源集合中，以供更多人阅读和讨论。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于《Wall-E》对《The Machine Stops》的改编是否过于乐观，以及对技术依赖问题的处理是否现实。

• **技术与文明的讨论**：
  - [simpaticoder] 提出一个假设，即不同社区可以根据技术水平选择生活方式，以增强文明韧性，并认为人们高估了在紧急情况下“降低技术水平”的能力。
  - [jaydenmilne] 质疑故事的核心是关于技术还是文明，认为“机器”可能象征着其他人类。

• **故事的历史与文化影响**：
  - [detourdog] 强调故事反映了人类长久以来的野心和对技术的追求。
  - [jodrellblank] 引用故事中的细节，讨论了现代社会对新想法的态度，并将故事中的概念与现实世界的现象（如社交媒体通知和城市规划）联系起来。

• **个人体验与推荐**：
  - [BiraIgnacio] 和 [stuartd] 分享了通过播客和BBC Radio 4改编接触到这个故事的经历。
  - [kimfc] 和 [sometimes_all] 提到这个故事是受Jaron Lanier推荐的，并且是他们心目中的优秀科幻推荐。
  - [rexarex] 认为这是对互联网的首次预测，并且至今仍有现实意义。

补充讨论：

  - [6510] 提到1966年的《Out of the Unknown》改编版本，提供了观看链接。
  
• **社区与收藏的建议**：

data.title: A lost decade chasing distributed architectures for data analytics?
data.author: andreasha
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了是否在追逐分布式数据分析架构的过程中，我们是否忽略了单节点计算能力的潜力，导致“失去十年”。作者使用2012年的MacBook Pro运行DuckDB数据库，测试其在处理大数据集时的性能。结果显示，尽管这台旧笔记本只有16GB内存，但它成功完成了所有TPC-H基准测试查询，尽管某些查询耗时较长。文章指出，2012年的硬件已具备相当的数据处理能力，可能本可以更早实现当前的数据革命，而不必过度依赖分布式系统。这表明，硬件发展速度可能超过了数据增长速度，单节点架构在许多情况下已足够应对大数据分析任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于大数据处理工具和技术的优劣比较，以及对小型数据工具的讨论

不同观点：
• braza和twic认为，使用命令行工具或小型数据库（如DuckDB）可以比Hadoop、Spark等分布式系统更高效，尤其是在处理中小型数据时。他们引用了相关文章和论文来支持这一观点，认为过去十年可能走错了方向，过度依赖了复杂的分布式系统。
• rr808和Mortiffer从实际工作经验出发，认为在实际工作中使用Scala、Spark等工具开发和运行速度慢，而R语言及其相关的数据处理包（如dplyr、DataTable）更高效且易于使用。
• zkmon强调，数据库的选择不仅仅是基于查询性能，还需要考虑数据库在公司文化、流程、工作流、协作等方面的作用。数据库需要适应整个生态系统，而不仅仅是数据量和查询速度。
• bhouston和willvarfar分享了他们的实际应用经验，认为像BigQuery和DuckDB这样的工具在实时交互式分析和探索性数据分析中表现优异，提供了快速和自由的分析体验。
• npalli对DuckDB的适用范围提出了质疑，认为DuckDB仅适用于小型数据集和读多写少的场景，对于需要实时更新和多用户并发写入的场景并不适合。

补充讨论：
• culebron21分享了一个关于分布式数据库的设想和思考，提出了客户端和服务器角色的转换以及数据查询冲突的问题。
• simlevesque寻求计算资源的帮助，以继续其使用DuckDB的研究项目。
• fulafel提供了更多关于大数据基准测试的参考资料。
• hodgesrm对慢查询的容忍度提出了质疑，认为在很多应用场景中，用户需要在毫秒级或秒级得到查询结果，这需要硬件的支持，尤其是当数据集很大且需要进行实时数据处理时，分布式系统是不可避免的选择。
• PotatoNinja分享了一个关于Small Data的视频，进一步丰富了讨论的内容。

争议焦点：
• 大数据处理工具（如Hadoop、Spark）和小型数据工具（如DuckDB、R）之间的选择和适用场景。
• 查询性能和整个数据库生态系统的适应性之间的权衡。
• 实时查询和慢查询的容忍度及其对实际应用的影响。

44027690.article_content:
The Lost Decade of Small Data?
Hannes Mühleisen
Published on
2025-05-19
Reading time: 9 minutes
TL;DR: We benchmark DuckDB on a 2012 MacBook Pro to decide: did we lose a decade chasing distributed architectures for data analytics?
Much has been said, not in the very least by ourselves, about how
data is actually not that “Big”
and how the speed of hardware innovation is outpacing the growth of useful datasets. We may have gone so far to
predict a data singularity in the near future
, where 99% of useful datasets can be comfortably queried on a single node. As
recently shown
, the median scan in Amazon Redshift and Snowflake reads a doable 100 MB of data, and the 99.9-percentile reads less than 300 GB. So the singularity might be closer than we think.
But we started wondering, when did this development really start? When did personal computers like the ubiquitous MacBook Pro, usually condemned to running Chrome, become the data processing powerhouses that they really are today?
Let's turn our attention to the
2012
Retina MacBook Pro
, a computer many people (myself included) bought at the time because of its gorgeous “Retina” display. Millions were sold. Despite being unemployed at the time, I had even splurged for the 16 GB RAM upgrade. But there was another often-forgotten revolutionary change in this machine: it was the first MacBook with a built-in Solid-State Disk (SSD)
and
a competitive
4-core 2.6 GHz “Core i7” CPU
. It's funny to watch the
announcement
again, where they
do
stress the performance aspect of the “all-flash architecture” as well.
Side note: the MacBook Air was actually the first MacBook with an (optional) built-in SSD already back in 2008. But it did not have the CPU firepower of the Pro, sadly.
Coincidentally, I still have this laptop in the
DuckDB Labs
office, currently used by my kids to type their names in a massive font size or watch Bluey on YouTube when they're around. But can this relic still run modern-day DuckDB? How will its performance compare to modern MacBooks? And could we have had the data revolution that we are seeing now already back in 2012? Let's find out!
Software
First, what about the operating system? In order to make the comparison fair(er) to the decades, we actually
downgraded
the operating system on the Retina to OS X 10.8.5 “Mountain Lion”, the operating system version that shipped just a few weeks after the laptop itself in July 2012. Even though the Retina can actually run 10.15 (Catalina), we felt a true 2012 comparison should also use an operating system from the era. Below is a screenshot of the user interface for those of us who sometimes feel a little old.
Moving on to DuckDB itself: here at DuckDB we are more than a little religious about portability and dependencies – or rather the lack thereof. This means that very little had to happen to make DuckDB run on the ancient Mountain Lion: the stock DuckDB binary is built with by default with backwards-compatibility to OS X 11.0 (Big Sur), but simply changing the flag and recompiling turned out to be enough to make DuckDB 1.2.2 run on Mountain Lion. We would have loved to also use a 2012 compiler to build DuckDB, but, alas, C++ 11 was unsurprisingly simply
too new
in 2012 to be fully supported by compilers. Either way, the binary runs fine and could have been also produced by working around the compiler bugs. Or we could have just hand-coded Assembly like
others have done
.
Benchmarks
But we're not interested in synthetic CPU scores, we're interested in
synthetic SQL scores
instead! To see how the old machine is holding up when performing
serious
data crunching, we used the
at this point rather tired but well-known TPC-H benchmark
at scale factor 1000. This means that the two main tables,
lineitem
and
orders
contain 6 and 1.5 Billion rows, respectively. When stored as a DuckDB database, the database has a size of ca. 265 GB.
From the
audited results on the TPC website
, we can see that running the benchmark on this scale factor on a single node seems to require hardware costing hundreds of thousands of Dollars.
We ran each of the 22 benchmark queries five times, and took the median runtime to remove noise. However, because the amount of RAM (16 GB) is very much less than the database size (256 GB), no significant amount of the input data can be cached in the buffer manager, so those are not really what people sometimes call “hot” runs.

data.title: A Formal Proof of Complexity Bounds on Diophantine Equations
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在Isabelle/HOL中对有界复杂度的丢番图方程进行形式化验证的通用构造。作者通过形式化验证，确认了在特定变量数和次数限制下，丢番图方程的不可判定性。这一工作扩展了Isabelle中多变量多项式的理论，并为处理复杂多项式定义提供了元编程基础设施。研究展示了数学家与计算机协作的潜力，通过定理证明器大大推进了研究进程。文章共16页，包含一个图示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MRDP定理及其相关未解问题和实际应用

不同观点：
• [kevinventullo] 强调MRDP定理的一个惊人结果，即存在一个多变量多项式，其第一个变量的整数解对应的值恰好是素数集合。他提供了一个链接，指向有关素数公式的维基百科页面，以支持其观点。

• [MJGrzymek] 认为未解的问题中，哪些（变量数量，次数）组合对于MRDP是不可判定的，这一问题被低估了。他提出，这些组合的答案是有限的，并且可以列举出最小的不可判定组合。如果限制变量数量、次数以及系数的最大绝对值，那么这个问题是可判定的，因为有限性决定了可判定性。

• [btilly] 提供了一个更易理解的总结，指出任何丢番图方程可以被简化为最多11个变量且次数最高约为10^63的方程。对于这一类丢番图方程，没有算法可以决定其在有理数范围内的可解性。

补充讨论：
• [nine_k] 提出了一个实际应用的问题，询问MRDP定理的这一结果是否对密码学有任何实际影响。

• [badmonster] 对MRDP定理的形式化工作表示赞赏，认为这是深度数论和形式方法之间的一项令人印象深刻的桥梁工作。

争议焦点：
- 目前讨论中没有明显的对立观点，但存在对MRDP定理未解问题的不同关注点，一些人关注理论上的不可判定性（MJGrzymek），另一些人则关注实际应用和理解（btilly, nine_k）。

总结：
讨论围绕MRDP定理的惊人结果、未解问题的不可判定性、以及其在密码学中的潜在应用展开。参与者对定理的理论意义和实际应用价值有不同侧重的讨论。

Title:
A Formal Proof of Complexity Bounds on Diophantine Equations
Authors:
Jonas Bayer
,
Marco David
View a PDF of the paper titled A Formal Proof of Complexity Bounds on Diophantine Equations, by Jonas Bayer and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a universal construction of Diophantine equations with bounded complexity in Isabelle/HOL. This is a formalization of our own work in number theory.
Hilbert's Tenth Problem was answered negatively by Yuri Matiyasevich, who showed that there is no general algorithm to decide whether an arbitrary Diophantine equation has a solution. However, the problem remains open when generalized to the field of rational numbers, or contrarily, when restricted to Diophantine equations with bounded complexity, characterized by the number of variables $\nu$ and the degree $\delta$. If every Diophantine set can be represented within the bounds $(\nu, \delta)$, we say that this pair is universal, and it follows that the corresponding class of equations is undecidable. In a separate mathematics article, we have determined the first non-trivial universal pair for the case of integer unknowns.
In this paper, we contribute a formal verification of the main construction required to establish said universal pair. In doing so, we markedly extend the Isabelle AFP entry on multivariate polynomials, formalize parts of a number theory textbook, and develop classical theory on Diophantine equations in Isabelle. Additionally, our work includes metaprogramming infrastructure designed to efficiently handle complex definitions of multivariate polynomials. Our mathematical draft has been formalized while the mathematical research was ongoing, and benefitted largely from the help of the theorem prover. We reflect how the close collaboration between mathematician and computer is an uncommon but promising modus operandi.

data.author: randomor

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款新推出的多功能书签和剪贴板管理应用的反馈和建议

不同观点：
• **用户界面和用户体验的简化与优化**：[allenu] 认为应用的登陆页面文字过长，建议简化并突出用户受益点，例如使用类似 "Save everything easily" 的短语。他还提到快捷键操作中，搜索框未自动对焦导致的小摩擦。[stevelacy] 补充建议隐藏主窗口的应用标题，使操作更简洁。

• **快捷键设计**：[kstrauser] 对 "Cmd + C twice" 的快捷键设计提出疑问，认为表达不够直观，并询问是否存在其他更便捷的快捷键选项。[raydenvm] 对该快捷键选择表示好奇，并询问是否考虑过其他可能的快捷键组合。

• **定价模式的争议**：[kstrauser] 认为该应用的定价较高，并将其与PastePal和GoodLinks进行比较，认为性价比不够吸引人。[asadm] 也表示更倾向于一次性收费模式，而非订阅制。

• **跨平台支持的需求**：[Jotalea] 和 [loremm] 都提到希望应用能够支持Linux系统，甚至表示愿意接受一些不那么无缝的解决方案。

• **与其他工具的比较**：[butz] 指出“稍后阅读”工具普遍存在用户不主动阅读的问题。[mnming] 则表示自己更倾向于使用Notion和Obsidian来管理书签，质疑是否值得使用专门工具。

• **隐私和数据安全**：[kstrauser] 对应用不收集用户数据的隐私政策表示赞赏。

• **信息透明度**：[G1N] 提到定价信息在网站上不明确，用户需要到App Store查看。 [awaseem] 同样表示不清楚应用是否免费，建议提高信息透明度。

补充讨论：
• **集成与扩展性**：[stevelacy] 建议应用可以与Raycast集成，提升使用效率。[jonator] 则询问是否支持MCP服务器。

• **命名和品牌认知**：[mdonahoe] 对应用名称 "Copycopy" 提出简单疑问，可能觉得名称容易引起混淆。

争议焦点：
• **定价过高与收费模式的争议**：部分用户认为应用的定价偏高且倾向于订阅制，不如其他类似工具性价比高，反映了用户对订阅制的普遍抵触情绪。

data.title: Show HN: Genetic Boids Web Simulation
data.author: vimgrinder
data.article_summary: 《GeneticBoids》是一篇关于模拟群体行为（Boids）的参数设置说明，由@attentionmech编写。文章描述了一个包含500个Boid个体的群体，具有不同的运动参数、群体行为规则（如对齐、分离、凝聚）、感知范围、遗传信号机制及视觉表现设置。Boid的寿命设定为2000，遗传信号的概率为0.002，范围为50，信号力为0.1，基因组长度为6。此外，还提供了多种预设模式（如 calm、chaotic、swarm 等）和性能调节选项（如网格大小、帧率目标）。文章最后列出了一些动态统计数据如FPS、活跃信号、平均速度、集群数量等，并提供了多种控制按钮如重置、随机化等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Boids模拟、颜色感知、技术实现与优化、用户体验与问题反馈

不同观点：
• [talkingtab] 提到Boids模拟的原创性来源于Craig Reynolds，并指出其早期Java版本的运动效果更为逼真。他认为当前版本虽然不错，但缺乏早期版本的真实感。他还对代码中的适应度函数进行了简单分析，提出了是否仅通过boids的距离来评价适应度。

• [chachacharge] 讨论了颜色感知问题，指出人类眼睛对绿色光更敏感，因为视觉系统对绿色光的波长反应最强，这与Boids模拟中颜色的使用无直接关系，但提供了颜色选择的科学背景。

• [brodo] 分享了自己使用Go和WebGPU实现的Boids模拟，能够在M1 Mac Pro上运行16k的boids，且尚未进行任何优化，展示了技术上的成就。

• [isoprophlex] 表达了对作品的高度赞赏，认为其视觉效果非常出色。

• [Xevion] 赞扬了作品的简洁和技术实现，同时提出了一些改进建议，包括颜色、交互性、时间控制和GPU优化，并提供了具体的技术参考（Sebastian Lague的视频）。

• [vladde] 提到一个类似的生命行为模拟视频，强调了通过简单规则创造复杂行为的现象，提供了相关视频链接。

• [anigbrowl] 反馈了在使用Vivaldi浏览器时遇到的问题，指出模拟在大约30秒后崩溃，提供了用户体验中的技术问题。

• [kldavis4] 询问了遗传算法在Boids模拟中的应用，表现出对技术细节的兴趣。

• [brulard] 对“信号”一词感到困惑，提出了定义上的问题。

• [rvnx] 表达了对Boids概念的新鲜感和喜爱。

• [throw_m239339] 提到曾在Blender中见过Boids，并指出对其设置理解不足但效果不错，提供了Boids在其他软件中的应用实例。

补充讨论：
• Boids模拟的真实感是讨论的焦点之一，talkingtab对不同版本的效果进行了比较。
• 技术实现和优化是另一个重要话题，brodo和Xevion分享了优化经验和建议。
• 用户体验反馈主要集中在anigbrowl提出的崩溃问题和kldavis4对遗传算法应用的疑问。
• 颜色选择和视觉效果得到了isoprophlex和chachacharge的关注，提出了科学和美学上的见解。

data.title: Show HN: I built a more productive way to manage AI chats
data.author: tapeo
data.article_summary: ContextChat是一款支持从网页、文件和GitHub导入内容并构建知识库的AI聊天工具。其主要功能包括：多项目和多聊天管理、持久化知识库、智能内容提取、灵活选择AI模型以及按需付费的信用系统。与传统工具相比，ContextChat无需手动复制粘贴，支持免费AI模型，无需信用卡即可开始使用，并允许在聊天中轻松切换AI模型。该工具提供简单定价，无订阅陷阱，帮助用户高效管理和查询项目信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何为开发者社区创建和管理API和库的上下文包，以及该想法的商业潜力和技术实现。

不同观点：
• [npollock] 提议创建包含流行API和库的上下文包，保持更新，并通过公共URL提供，以成为开发者社区的可信上下文资源库，从而吸引流量和潜在商机。
• [wewewedxfgdf] 提到Gemini AI Studio提供的1百万token窗口和上传整个代码库的功能，使得他对自己类似的项目失去了兴趣。
• [J_cst] 推荐RooCode，并表示从Cline迁移到RooCode后效果不错，特别是在任务中切换代理和模型。
• [jeswin] 认为现有的UI/app可以通过代理流解决上下文问题，并指出由于现有应用的“粘性”，用户不太可能轻易迁移到新应用，即使是商业产品。
• [jmcmaster] 关注数据上传的隐私和安全问题，表示由于这些顾虑，无法在工作中使用此类工具。
• [iankp] 提到NotebookLM可能已经是类似的产品，并询问选择模型和自定义上下文功能的差异化。
• [imranq] 建议只做上下文而不连接到任何模型，通过集成驱动器文件夹、GitHub等生成最佳上下文，然后复制到用户选择的模型或工作流。
• [argestes] 对接收更新邮件列表感兴趣。
• [fernly] 提到Claude Projects可能是类似的产品。
• [scottward] 关心Google Docs的自动同步功能，询问是否计划实现自动重新同步。
• [tapeo] 分享了自己解决从聊天到聊天复制起始上下文的经验，通过生成基础上下文来开始新聊天。
• [esafak] 认为该UX与You.com相似。
• [artichaud1] 表示喜欢这个想法，并打算尝试。
• [dangus] 幽默地指出工作性质正在从实际工作转向管理AI做工作，因此需要管理工具来管理如何告诉AI做工作。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于新产品与现有产品（如Gemini AI Studio、NotebookLM、Claude Projects）的差异化和竞争力。
- 功能实现上的讨论集中在数据自动同步、隐私和安全问题以及模型的选择和集成。
- 用户对现有应用的依赖和“粘性”被认为是新产品推广的一个挑战。
- 对产品UX设计和功能实现的具体建议，如邮件列表更新、自动同步功能等，也提供了产品改进的方向。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一份关于镜头设计形式的终极指南，涵盖了各种光学系统及其应用。文章探讨了基本和重要的镜头设计形式，包括单透镜、双透镜、三合透镜、天塞透镜、双高斯透镜等，并解释了它们的发展和用途。文章还讨论了现代镜头设计，如非球面镜头、自由曲面镜头和用于手机摄像头的镜头，以及特殊用途的镜头系统，如鱼眼镜头、变焦镜头和反射光学镜头。此外，文章提供了对镜头设计背后原理的深入理解，帮助读者在面对规格表时更好地选择和设计镜头。文章最后还提到使用计算软件进行镜头设计的现代方法。
data.comments_summary:

Overview
This is an Ultimate Guide of lens design forms, the optical systems that are used in our world.
The basic lens design forms are in here, and we can take a deep look into the development of lens design. But the not all the lens designs are simple lenses, we will look at newer and important lens design forms as well.
You’d be surprised to see what lenses are related to one another, and how we can break down seemingly complex lens design into parts from different lens forms.

data.title: Japan and the Birth of Modern Shipbuilding
data.author: m463
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了日本如何在二战后吸收美国战时快速造船技术，并发展出现代造船业。二战期间，美国通过焊接和预制件组装的方法迅速建造大量船只，但战后这一体系被解散。美国实业家如亨利·凯瑟和丹尼尔·路德维希将这一技术带到日本，特别是在吴市造船厂进行大型油轮的建造。吴市曾是二战时建造世界上最大战舰“大和号”的地方，拥有先进的设施。路德维希在吴建造了一系列破纪录的大型油轮，包括1958年世界上首个超过10万吨的“宇宙阿波罗号”。通过结合预制件、焊接和工业流程改进策略，日本发展出更快、更便宜的现代造船方法，最终主导了全球造船市场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本与美国在战后造船业的比较及其对经济和技能发展的影响

不同观点：
• DrNosferatu认为，欧盟当前的自由经济理论强调国家不应干预经济，但这一点应该重新审视，特别是在了解了日本战后造船业的成功经验后。
• alephnerd指出，日本战后造船业的薪资相对于全国平均水平较高，约为160%，这吸引了高技能工人进入该行业。相比之下，美国和加拿大在同时期没有类似的薪资差距。日本将造船业视为工程/STEM学科，而美国则视为蓝领半技能职业。alephnerd还提到，类似的趋势在韩国以及其他行业（如芯片设计、VFX、电池制造等）中也能观察到。他还比较了美国与以色列、印度及中东欧在教育系统上的不同，后者更注重系统和架构基础。
• dumdedum123对alephnerd的观点持怀疑态度，认为美国在二战期间发明了现代造船技术，而日本只是复制并发展了这些技术。

补充讨论：
• rufus_foreman提供了数据支持，指出在战争高峰期，美国生产了全球近90%的船舶，但到1950年代，这一比例下降到略高于2%。这一数据为讨论提供了历史背景，说明美国在造船业的显著变化。
• alephnerd的观点引用了多个来源支持其论点，包括关于日本战后薪资的数据和关于造船业工程学科定位的历史文章。
• 争议的焦点在于日本造船业的成功是否主要归因于复制美国技术并加以发展，还是由于其他因素（如薪资激励、技能水平等）推动了其成功。

总结：评论主要围绕日本与美国在战后造船业的发展路径及其对技能和经济的影响展开讨论。alephnerd强调了薪资和技能对行业发展的影响，而dumdedum123则质疑日本是否仅仅是复制了美国的技术。rufus_foreman的数据提供了对美国造船业历史变化的补充视角。

Universe Apollo, first 100,000 DWT supertanker, built by National Bulk Carriers at Kure, Japan.
During WWII, the US constructed an unprecedented shipbuilding machine. By assembling ships from welded, prefabricated blocks, the US built a huge number of cargo ships incredibly quickly, overwhelming Germany’s u-boats and helping to win the war. But when the war was over, this shipbuilding machine was dismantled. Industrialists like Henry Kaiser and Stephen Bechtel, who operated some of the US’s most efficient wartime shipyards, left the shipbuilding business. Prior to the war, the US had been an uncompetitive commercial shipbuilder producing a small fraction of commercial oceangoing ships, and that’s what it became again. At the height of the war the US was producing nearly 90% of the world’s ships. By the 1950s, it produced just over 2%.
But the lessons from the US’s shipbuilding machine weren’t forgotten. After the war, practitioners brought them to Japan, where they would continue to evolve, eventually allowing Japan to build ships faster and cheaper than almost anyone else in the world.
Origins of Japan’s post-war shipbuilding industry
One of the shipyards that built cargo ships during the war was
Welding Shipyards
, owned by Daniel Ludwig. In 1936 Ludwig had founded shipping company National Bulk Carriers (NBC), which bought surplus WWI cargo ships and converted them into oil tankers. From there, Ludwig expanded into shipbuilding, and built his one-berth shipyard at Norfolk in 1940.
1
During the war, Welding Shipyards produced T3 tankers using prefabricated welded construction, which were then operated by National Bulk Carriers. After the war, Ludwig continued to build tankers: between 1948 and 1950 he built 5
Bulkpetrol-class tankers
, then the largest tankers in the world.
Ludwig wanted to build even larger ships, in part to capitalize on the burgeoning iron ore trade with Venezuela, but was limited by the size of the berth at Welding Shipyards. Unfazed, Ludwig dispatched his lieutenant Elmer Hann to find a shipyard with the capacity to build larger vessels. The search brought Hann to a former naval shipyard in Kure, Japan, near Hiroshima. The Kure facilities were enormous: they had been used to build the
Yamato
, the largest battleship in the world, and had a 100-ton gantry crane and a drydock capable of building ships of 150,000 tons deadweight. (By comparison, a Liberty ship is about 10,800 deadweight tons.) In 1951, Ludwig signed a 10-year lease for the Kure shipyard.
At Kure, National Bulk Carriers built a series of record-breakingly large ships: the 38,000 deadweight ton Petro Kure in 1952, the 45,000 deadweight ton Phoenix in 1954, and the 55,000 deadweight ton Sinclair Petro-Lore in 1955. The
Universe Apollo
, launched at Kure in 1958, was the first tanker in the world to exceed 100,000 deadweight tons. Altogether Ludwig built 42 ships at Kure, many of them the largest in the world when completed. When his lease at Kure expired, the shipyards were acquired by Japanese shipbuilder IHI, which continued to build enormous tankers for Ludwig.
Kure and modern shipbuilding methods
Modern shipbuilding methods were born at Kure in the 1950s, by combining three different strategies for industrial process improvement.
The first strategy was the prefabricated, welded shipbuilding methods that the US had used so successfully during WWII. To briefly recap, prior to WWII ships were largely built in-place by riveting together the hull one piece at a time. This was time-consuming (a Liberty-sized ship could take months to produce) and labor-intensive, in part because riveting took a long time, and in part because so much of the work was done in the confines of the partially-built ship. Replacing riveting with welding allowed for faster assembly, and also saved steel (since welded plates didn’t need to overlap like riveted plates did). And by constructing the ship out of large, prefabricated blocks, work could be moved out of the confines of the ship and into specialized assembly areas where it could be more easily performed and more workers could work on the ship at once, increasing speed and improving efficiency.
Prefabricated block being lifted into place at Oregonship during WWII.
Both Elmer Hann and Danield Ludwig were well-versed in welded, prefabricated shipbuilding. Ludwig had used it at Welding Shipyards to build T3 and Bulkpetrol-class tankers, and Elmer Hann had been the superintendent for Henry Kaiser’s
Swan Island shipyard
, which used welded, prefabricated construction to produce 147 T2 tankers ov

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Hacker News的一个替代时间线界面（hcker.news），用户可以自定义新闻的展示方式和过滤条件。用户可以选择不同的视图模式（如经典、Hckr、多列），调整主题（浅色、深色等），设置字体大小和密度。此外，还提供高级过滤选项，可以根据标题包含或排除特定关键词，并设置最小投票数来筛选故事。该界面旨在提升用户体验，尤其适合关注独立网络内容的读者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News及其替代前端的用户体验和功能改进

不同观点：
• **支持Hacker News稳定性和开放数据的优点**：
  - jasonthorsness认为Hacker News的核心优势在于其稳定性，链接自2007年以来几乎没有失效，同时对外开放数据，支持第三方创建替代界面，这种用户友好的做法与互联网其他部分的封闭趋势形成对比。

• **介绍和展示自建替代前端的功能**：
  - adrianwaj介绍了自己创建的Hackerbrain网站，强调其快速查看顶部评论和切换评论视图的功能，并对这些功能感到满意。
  - coolwulf分享了自己用Rust构建的开源Hacker News客户端，展示了该客户端的独特性。
  - wvl建议参考hckrnews.com，并提供了一个暗色模式的链接。
  
• **对无JavaScript体验的批评和建议**：
  - koito17指出Hackerbrain网站在禁用JavaScript后完全无法使用，而Hacker News官方前端在这方面处理得更好。建议进行服务器端数据获取以避免页面闪烁，并让用户在JavaScript加载前至少能看到标题。

• **对UI/UX设计的赞赏**：
  - ls-a赞赏Hacker News的UI/UX设计多年无人能及，并询问是否由专业设计师设计。
  
• **功能缺失和建议**：
  - nico表示希望有一个隐藏功能，以便清理已读或不感兴趣的内容。
  - feep询问是否计划加入RSS支持，并感谢hnrss.github.io的创建者，同时表达了对更多过滤功能的期望。
  
• **对随机浏览功能的推荐**：
  - atomic128推荐使用随机浏览功能，认为这是阅读Hacker News的最佳方式，可以避免成瘾性和个人偏见，提供了具体网站https://rnsaffn.com/zg2/作为示例。

• **对自定义配置的需求**：
  - adrianwaj希望看到类似/bestcomments的功能，并询问是否已有类似功能存在。
  - conroydave建议将设置作为URL参数，以便用户可以书签他们的首选配置。

补充讨论：
• **对减少在线时间的需求**：
  - _august表示作为一个试图减少在线时间但仍想保持更新的人，非常喜欢这些替代前端提供的功能。

争议焦点：
• **JavaScript依赖性**：
  - koito17认为Hackerbrain网站在无JavaScript环境下的表现不佳，而官方前端处理得更好，这是功能改进的一个争议点。

• **功能需求差异**：
  - 用户对隐藏功能、RSS支持、自定义配置等功能的需求不同，反映出不同用户在使用Hacker News时的偏好和优先级不同。

data.title: The Transwedge Product
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了超越楔积（transwedge product）的概念，作为几何积的完全分解方法。几何积通常被表示为楔积和点积的组合，但对于高阶元素，几何积会产生更多项。文章首先回顾了几何积、楔积和交换积的定义，指出这些在高阶情况下不够用。为了解决这个问题，作者提出了超越楔积，它通过一个参数 \( k \) 来控制，并使用格拉斯曼代数的基本操作（如楔积、左右补、以及度量的应用）来定义。超越楔积公式为：

\[
\mathbf{a} \underset{k}{\unicode{x2A53}} \mathbf{b} = \sum_{\mathbf{c} \in \mathcal{B}_k} (\mathbf{\underline{c}} \vee \mathbf{a}) \wedge (\mathbf{b} \vee \mathbf{c^{\unicode{x2605}}})
\]

其中，\(\mathcal{B}_k\) 是所有阶为 \( k \) 的基元素的集合。公式通过遍历基元素并结合左右补和楔积来分解几何积，使其适用于任意多向量。超越楔积不仅能替代交换积，还能生成几何积的所有可能项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：几何代数与传统外代数和微分形式在物理学中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• **几何代数没有明显优势**：[senderista]认为几何代数相对于外代数和微分形式在物理学中并没有显著优势。他提到几乎所有理论物理学家都持类似观点，并质疑是否遗漏了某些关键点。

• **几何代数的优势在于统一性**：[algebraphys]认为几何代数的优势在于它能够统一和简化不同数学结构的处理。例如，几何代数可以将旋转、反射等变换统一在一个框架内，从而简化计算。

• **应用场景不同**：[physics101]指出几何代数和外代数各有其适用的场景。几何代数在处理某些具体问题（如计算机图形学和机器人学）中表现突出，而外代数和微分形式在传统物理学理论中更为普遍和成熟。

• **教学和普及问题**：[educheck]认为几何代数未被广泛采纳的一个原因可能是教育和普及的不足。很多物理学家在学校里主要学习外代数和微分形式，对几何代数的理解和应用相对陌生。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**在于几何代数是否真的提供了超越传统方法的实际优势。一方认为其统一性和简化性是重要优势，另一方则认为传统方法已经足够成熟和广泛应用，新方法的推广和学习成本可能不值得。

• **论据和例子**：支持几何代数的人提到其在具体应用（如计算机图形学和机器人学）中的成功案例，而反对者则认为传统物理学中并没有广泛需求去替换现有的成熟方法。

• **教育的作用**：有评论指出，几何代数的普及程度可能与其在物理学中的应用广度有关，教育体系的影响不可忽视。

The Transwedge Product
Eric Lengyel   •   May 23, 2025
Introductory texts on geometric algebra often begin by showing how the geometric product is a combination of the wedge product and the dot product,
giving us the formula
[1]
\(\mathbf a \mathbin{\unicode{x27D1}} \mathbf b = \mathbf a \wedge \mathbf b + \mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b\).
(1)
However, the above formula holds only for
vectors
\(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\). When \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\)
are allowed to assume values of higher grade, the geometric product generally yields more terms, especially in higher dimensions. When the operands
have grades \(g\) and \(h\), the geometric product can generate a result containing terms having grades \(m\) ranging from \(|g - h|\) to \(g + h\)
such that the difference between each grade \(m\) and \(g + h\) is an even number. For example, the geometric product between two
bivectors
\(\mathbf A\) and \(\mathbf B\) in a 4D algebra generates components having grades 0, 2, and 4. We can decompose this product as
\(\mathbf A \mathbin{\unicode{x27D1}} \mathbf B = \mathbf A \wedge \mathbf B + \mathbf A \times \mathbf B + \mathbf A \cdot \mathbf{\widetilde B}\),
(2)
where the \(\mathbf A \times \mathbf B\) term is called the
commutator product
, defined as \(\mathbf A \times \mathbf B = \mathbf A \mathbin{\unicode{x27D1}} \mathbf B - \mathbf B \mathbin{\unicode{x27D1}} \mathbf A\).
The commutator product corresponds to the grade-2 part of the geometric product in this case, but it generally produces more terms when the operands have higher grades.
Furthermore, because the commutator product is defined in terms of the geometric product, it can’t help us decompose the geometric product into
independent operations. That would be circular.
When one of the operands of the geometric product is a vector \(\mathbf a\), and the other operand is an arbitrary multivector \(\mathbf B\),
we can generalize Equation (1) a little bit as
\(\mathbf a \mathbin{\unicode{x27D1}} \mathbf B = \mathbf a \wedge \mathbf B + \mathbf B \unicode{x230A} \mathbf a\).
(3)
Here, the expression \(\mathbf B \unicode{x230A} \mathbf a\) is the
right contraction
, which is one of the interior products in Grassmann algebra.
The right contraction is defined as \(\mathbf B \unicode{x230A} \mathbf a = \mathbf B \vee \mathbf a^{\unicode{x2605}}\), where the superscript \(\unicode{x2605}\)
denotes the right dual.
[2]
When the operands of the contraction have the same grade, it reduces to the inner product, so we end up
right back where we started if we insert a vector for \(\mathbf B\).
What would be nice to have is a general formula that gives us each possible term generated by the geometric product using only the fundamental operations of Grassmann algebra.
These operations are the exterior (wedge) product, the left and right complements, and an application of the metric. All other operations in exterior algebra can be derived from
these primitives, and it is my intention to demonstrate that the geometric product can be as well. The general formula that we’re looking for would need to generate a spectrum
of products that include the exterior product on one end and the interior product (contraction) on the other end as well as anything that could arise in between. This formula would
not only be able to replace the commutator product above but also give us every term of every geometric product between operands of higher grades.
I would like to introduce the
transwedge product
, which is the result of my search for a way to completely decompose the geometric product.
[3]
The transwedge product is parameterized by an order \(k\), and it is denoted by the upward double wedge symbol \(\unicode{x2A53}\) with a subscript or underscript indicating that order.
[4]
The transwedge product is defined for arbitrary multivectors \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf b\) as
\(\displaystyle \mathbf a \mathbin{\underset{k}{\unicode{x2A53}}} \mathbf b = \sum_{\mathbf c \in \mathcal B_k}{(\mathbf{\underline c} \vee \mathbf a) \wedge (\mathbf b \vee \mathbf c^{\unicode{x2605}})}\).
(4)
It may look like there’s a lot going on in this formula, but it’s actually pretty straightforward stuff.
First, \(\mathcal B_k\) is the set of all basis elements having grade \(k\). For example, in three dimensions, \(\mathcal B_0 = \{\mathbf 1\}\), \(\mathcal B_1 = \{\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \mathbf e_3\}\),
\(\mathcal B_2 = \{\mathbf e_{23}, \mathbf e_{31}, \mathbf e_{12}\}\), and \(\mathcal B_3 = \{\mathbf e_{123}\}\). The sum is taken over all basis elements in the set \(\mathcal B_k\),
and each summand is a wedge product of something involving \(\mathbf a\) on the left and something involving \(\mathbf b\) on the right. The left operand, \(\mathbf{\underline c} \vee \mathbf a\),
is the left complement of \(\mathbf c\) within the subspace spanned by the factors of \(\mathbf a\), with the sign set so that \((\mathbf{\underline c} \vee \mathbf a) \wedge \mathbf c = \mathbf a\).

data.title: Emacs dired-mode as a file manager
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Guix系统中使用Emacs的Dired模式作为文件管理器，解决文件类型与默认程序关联的问题。作者平时依赖Emacs处理文件，不常使用传统的文件管理器。当从网上下载文件并点击“显示文件夹”时，由于缺少文件管理器，没有任何反应。为解决此问题，作者通过Guix的`home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type`服务配置，将目录的MIME类型`inode/directory`与Emacs的Dired模式关联起来。具体操作包括编写Guile Scheme配置文件，定义一个`.desktop`文件并关联到指定MIME类型，最终实现用Emacs管理文件。通过`guix home reconfigure`命令应用配置，成功解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs中的Dired模式及其功能和使用体验

不同观点：
• **Dired模式的优点**：
  - **批量操作和灵活性**：[susam] 强调Dired模式可以轻松标记、操作多个文件，进行批量复制、移动、删除、更改权限等操作，且操作流畅、直观，比标准Unix命令行工具更加方便。
  - **跨环境一致性**：[susam] 指出Dired模式的肌肉记忆和命令在不同系统（如macOS、Xfce4、KDE等）上具有一致性，无论本地还是远程登录，操作体验不变。
  - **脚本化与可记录性**：[susam] 提到Dired的所有操作都可以通过Elisp脚本化，或者通过键盘宏录制和重放，极大提升了自动化操作的可能性。

• **wdired模式的优点**：
  - **可编辑的Dired缓冲区**：[julienchastang], [entropie], [shwouchk] 都提到wdired模式，认为其最大亮点是可以直接在缓冲区中编辑文件名和权限，并通过简单的快捷键（如C-c C-c）提交更改，极大简化了批量文件名修改的过程。
  - **与Emacs其他功能的结合**：[shwouchk] 强调可以使用正则替换、多光标、宏等Emacs功能，进一步增强文件名批量编辑的灵活性。

• **Dired模式的局限与改进建议**：
  - **文件浏览体验不佳**：[ww520] 指出Dired模式默认的文件访问命令会在新窗口中打开文件，导致需要频繁关闭窗口，提出通过自定义Emacs配置解决此问题，并分享了自己的init.el配置代码。
  - **多文件名同时编辑的期待**：[90s_dev] 希望Dired-x模式能够支持像VS Code中的多光标一样同时编辑多个文件名，并希望有人能在Windows Explorer或VS Code中实现这一功能。

  - **积极观点**：[ews] 赞赏Emacs和Guix（或NixOS）的结合，认为可以通过简单的代码复制快速实现配置，令人惊叹。
  - **批评观点**：[paulyy_y] 认为将一切功能都塞进Emacs，甚至称其为操作系统的做法有些过头，表现出对Emacs万能化的质疑。

补充讨论：
• **跨平台操作的便捷性**：[susam] 强调了Dired模式在不同系统和环境中的一致性操作体验，这对跨平台用户来说是一个重要优势。
• **快捷键与功能扩展**：[julienchastang], [entropie], [shwouchk] 等人提到了快捷键操作和wdired模式下的编辑功能，显示出Dired模式在快捷操作和功能扩展上的潜力。

争议焦点：
• **Emacs万能化**：部分用户如[ews]对Emacs的强大功能和扩展性表示赞赏，而[paulyy_y]则认为将所有功能集成到Emacs中有些过度，表现出对这种万能化趋势的质疑。
• **文件浏览的体验问题**：[ww520] 提出的Dired模式下文件浏览的不便问题，以及其通过自定义配置解决此问题的方案，引发了一些对默认操作不便的讨论。

44075388.article_content:
LYNN
Fedi
|
Git
|
Emacs
Using Emacs as your file manager in Guix
The Problem
File managers. They manage your files. Some examples are windows explorer, GNOME's Nautilus, or Dolphin for KDE. If you are a real sicko and only use the terminal, you may be familiar with ranger as well.
They are a perceived necessity in modern-day computing with how easy they make moving, copying, and deleting files.
Well, I don't use any of those. It's not from any self-imposed rule, or a sense of superiority,I just simply forgot they exist.
Whenever I need to edit files, I have emacs. Whenever I need to open files, I have emacs. And whenever I need to delete files, well I tend to do that in the command-line. This is just how I have gotten comfortable working with documents and code and it has not brought on any real need for a file manager. My one exception is when I download something from the internet, and click
Show In Folder
. Nothing happens.
Programs on linux use a database called
xdg-mime
to match certain file types to default programs to handle them. On systems like GNOME or KDE, with full-fledged desktop environments, these are set to things that would make sense: images are opened in an image-viewer. Text files are opened in a text editor, and directories are opened in the file manager. This sounds like a lot of unique programs: an image viewer, a text editor,
and
a file manager? This problem of too-many-programs that I made up for myself is easily solved with a single program, emacs!
MIME stands for "Multi-purpose Internet Mail Extensions and looks something like
text/html
or
application/json
. If you do any work on the frontend of the web, you've encountered these!
The "Solution"
I'm sure some of you reading this are rolling your eyes or reciting the well-known "Emacs is a great OS, but …" I use it a lot, though. I already use
dired-mode
to manage my writing  and programming. It's something that is powerful, and comfortable to use. If you are following along and use something else, it is also quite easy to adjust my code here as well.
Ok, with that out of the way let's look at what we actually want to do: xdg-mime needs to connect "Opening a directory" with "opening emacs in
dired-mode
." First, we need the MIME type for directories. A quick search shows that it is called
inode/directory
.
I have no idea why it is called inode/directory, and I couldn't find an explanation. I've learned not to ask questions about these names.
Opening emacs in
dired-mode
is the easy part: if you pass emacs a directory instead of a file, it automatically opens in the appropriate mode. Great! Now we need to tie these two concepts together.
If we were using a non-declarative system, such as Debian, I would suggest doing something like creating a
.desktop
file, running
xdg-mime default emacs-dired.desktop inode/directory
and that would be it. You could theoretically do this on Guix as well. There is a big downside with this strategy, though: the changes you make are not documented anywhere on your system. If you wanted to duplicate your setup on a new laptop, for example, you would have to either note down this change you made or run into it again, hopefully remember your solution, and then reproduce it. Maybe this works for others, but I know myself. I will not remember, I will run into it again, and then I will get frustrated again. That's why we have
guix-home
configuration.
home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type
is a very helpful service in the
guix-home
configuration tool. It allows you to create
xdg-desktop-entry
for each
.desktop
file you would normally need to create, link those to the MIME type of your choice, and that's it. It is also all written down explicitly, so there is no confusion on what steps were taken. Let's look at the most basic example to solve our issue:
(home-environment
(services
(list
(service home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type
(home-xdg-mime-applications-configuration
(default '((inode/directory . emacs-dired.desktop)))
(desktop-entries
(list (xdg-desktop-entry
(file
"emacs-dired"
)
(name
"Emacs Dired as a file manager"
)
(type 'application)
(config
'((exec .
"emacsclient -c -a emacs %u"
)
(mimetype .
"inode/directory"
)))))))))))
If this is nonsense to you, I apologize. I'm definitely not the person who should be teaching you lisp. You should definitely learn it, though!  The configuration language for Guix is called
Guile Scheme
, read up on it.
I use
emacsclient
here because I have emacs always running as a daemon.
-c
tells it to create a new frame, and
-a emacs
tells it to fall-back to a regular emacs session if there is some reason my daemon has stopped running.
And that's it! It works perfectly after a quick
guix home reconfigure
.  To expand, just add a new
xdg-desktop-entry
that runs whatever script you wish, and then tie it to a MIME type in the
default
list.
I considered adding things for image types, text types, etc. This would be useful to do if you used a regular file manager. With emacs tho
44075388.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Guix系统中使用Emacs的Dired模式作为文件管理器，解决文件类型与默认程序关联的问题。作者平时依赖Emacs处理文件，不常使用传统的文件管理器。当从网上下载文件并点击“显示文件夹”时，由于缺少文件管理器，没有任何反应。为解决此问题，作者通过Guix的`home-xdg-mime-applications-service-type`服务配置，将目录的MIME类型`inode/directory`与Emacs的Dired模式关联起来。具体操作包括编写Guile Scheme配置文件，定义一个`.desktop`文件并关联到指定MIME类型，最终实现用Emacs管理文件。通过`guix home reconfigure`命令应用配置，成功解决问题。

主要讨论点：是否可以通过选择简朴的生活方式和搬到农村地区来解决现代住房和生活成本问题，以及这种生活方式是否可行和理想。

不同观点：
• **potato3732842的观点**：不认同作者的观点，认为生活成本高昂并不是因为人们不愿妥协，而是由于住房法律、法规、分区等问题。他以自己的生活为例，表明即使节省开支，租金和房贷的差距依然巨大。
• **aeturnum的观点**：部分同意作者的结论，认为当前确实是有史以来尝试实现美国梦的最佳时机，但前提是接受一种较为独立和孤立的生活方式，而这并不符合大多数人的期望。
• **xeromal的观点**：支持简朴生活，认为在远程工作普及的情况下，住在小城市或农村是更经济合理的选择，并且可以避免大城市的高生活成本和孤独感。
• **999900000999的观点**：质疑在没有汽车的情况下在农村生活的可行性，认为除非基本不出门，否则汽车是必需品，并提出使用二手自行车作为替代方案。
• **egypturnash的观点**：欣赏一些人能够适应并享受寒冷和长冬的气候，认为这样可以减少对自己偏好气候区域的竞争。
• **silisili的观点**：指出作者忽视了健康保险和 utilities 等其他高昂费用，认为这些会大幅增加生活成本。
• **Goronmon的观点**：以讽刺的语气评论作者对取暖计划的缺乏具体性。
• **kens的观点**：对文章中提到的 Moses-Saunders 国际水电大坝的历史背景进行了扩展，推荐阅读相关书籍。
• **Taikonerd的观点**：质疑在纽约州北部过冬的可行性，认为与在墨西哥的廉价生活相比，这种生活方式并不理想。
• **AndrewOMartin的观点**：强调健康问题在简朴生活中的潜在风险。
• **ydlr的观点**：认为文章在对比不同时代的生活方式时存在误导，指出现代人面临的结构性问题无法通过个体努力解决。
• **viccis的观点**：认为文章类似于“老人对云大喊”式的批评，指出文章的建议忽略了现代社会的期望和社会结构变化。
• **keiferski的观点**：支持以1960年代的生活标准生活，认为这样可以减少工作压力，但承认面临现代社会期望的挑战。
• **neilv的观点**：提到在美加边境附近的一些城镇的废弃状态，并联想到《使女的故事》中的情景，质疑这些地方的低廉房价背后的原因。
• **chasd00的观点**：认为现代科技如手机和Starlink使得在农村生活更为可行，减少了孤立感。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于现代人是否能够并且愿意接受一种简朴、独立的农村生活方式，以及这种生活方式是否真的能够解决高生活成本的问题。
• 讨论中多次提到结构性问题，如住房法律、法规、社会期望等，这些被认为是影响生活成本和选择的重要因素。
• 健康保险、取暖、交通等实际问题在简朴生活中被多次提及，显示出这些是影响生活方式可行性的重要因素。

data.title: Does Field Ordering Affect Model Performance?
data.author: kallyaleksiev
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了字段顺序是否会影响大型语言模型（LLM）的性能，特别是在使用Pydantic模型实现结构化输出的AI应用中。作者通过使用新推出的pydantic-evals框架，对绘画风格分类任务进行了实验，比较了两种字段顺序：一种是先输出答案再输出推理，另一种是先输出推理再输出答案。实验包括简单分类任务和更复杂的硬任务。结果显示，对于简单任务，不同字段顺序对模型性能影响不大；而对于硬任务，先输出推理的顺序在某些模型上表现更好。作者指出，LLM的行为难以完全预测，但关注这些细微模式和想法有助于理解其工作机制。完整代码可在GitHub上找到。

44051069.article_content:
Does Field Ordering Affect Model Performance?
I mostly wrote this post as an excuse to try the freshly-minted and excellent
pydantic-evals
framework for LLM evaluations but one interesting question that arises when working with
Pydantic Models
to implement structured output in your AI applications is:
What happens if you shuffle the order of fields in your schema?
Does it matter if your output type looks like this:
class AgentOutput(BaseModel):
answer: str
reasoning: str
or like this:
class AgentOutput(BaseModel):
reasoning: str
answer: str
One line of argument goes something like this:
For reasoning models, field ordering shouldn’t matter much. But for non-reasoning models, the second ordering might actually help: by placing the reasoning field first, we could nudge the model into a chain-of-thought-like regime early on, encouraging it to construct a more
well-grounded
answer. Contrast that with the first ordering, which asks the mode to output the answer first and then the explanation. This could backfire if the model locks in a wrong answer and the reasoning becomes a post-hoc rationalisation.
Well let's see!
Setup
We use the
painting style classification
task from HuggingFace (because it doesn't seem saturated from 0-shot models). We create two kinds of tasks — a simple classification one (just the standard task itself) and a
hard task
which does the following:
The model is given an image of a painting and a list of strings. The model first has to assign the painting a numerical label according to the style (as per the classical task) and then it has to select the string from the list
that has exactly i+2 letters
where i is the index of the label the model chose in the previous step.
This harder task seemingly requires more reasoning so one might expect techniques that elicit reasoning in non-reasoning models to perform better at it.
The
pydantic-evals
code for the creation of this task looks roughly like this:
import random
import string
from datasets import load_dataset
from pydantic_evals import Case, Dataset
from pydantic_evals.evaluators import EqualsExpected
PAINTING_DATASET = load_dataset("keremberke/painting-style-classification", "full")
LABEL_NAMES = PAINTING_DATASET["train"].features["labels"].names
AUXILIARY_LS = ["".join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=i)) for i in range(30)]
HARD_PYDANTIC_PAINTING_DATASET = Dataset[PIL.Image.Image, int](
cases=[
Case(
inputs=PAINTING_DATASET["test"][i]["image"],
expected_output=AUXILIARY_LS[PAINTING_DATASET["test"][i]["labels"] + 2],
)
for i in range(len(PAINTING_DATASET["test"]))
],
evaluators=[
EqualsExpected(),
],
)
We also need a framework / logic for structured output. By far my favourite framework for that and more is
pydantic ai
so we can define a few agents like so:
class HardTaskAgentOutputAnswerFirst(BaseModel):
answer: str
reasoning: str
ht_af_agent = Agent(
model=MODEL_NAME,

A World Turned Upside Down
Christopher Hill’s history from below.
Christopher Hill’s Revolutions
The radical life and work of the historian.
Peter Linebaugh
and
Marcus Rediker

Illustration by Joe Ciardiello.
This article appears in the
June 2025 issue
.
Christopher Hill was one of the most prolific and influential historians of the 20th century. He was also the product of two specific eras of political and social change: the Old Left’s communist and working-class movements of the 1930s and ’40s, and the New Left’s liberation and countercultural movements of the 1960s and ’70s.
At the end of the former, in 1940, Hill wrote
The English Revolution 1640
, which provided a class analysis of the bourgeois revolution against feudalism ﻿and charted a lifetime of scholarship ahead. In the middle of the latter, in 1972, Hill published another book on the same period, his most profound and lasting work,
The World Turned Upside Down: Radical Ideas During the English Revolution
. A social and intellectual history of religious radicals who pioneered the modern ideas and practices of democracy and equality, it was also a book that explored a commoners’ “revolution within the revolution” that, although it failed, nonetheless represented a deep origin story for the history of modern radicalism. Both books, inspired by the movements of their time, helped create the breakthrough that we have now come to call “history from below.”
Books in review
Christopher Hill: The Life of a Radical Historian
by
Michael Braddick
Buy this book
Over a career that spanned more than 60 years, Hill wrote 16 more books, dozens of articles, and seven collections of essays. Along the way, he became the leading interpreter of the English Revolution and its broader 17th century. He also covered an extraordinary range of topics, in books from
Economic Problems of the Church: From Archbishop Whitgift to the Long Parliament
(1956), through
Intellectual Origins of the English Revolution
(1965), to
The English Bible and the Seventeenth-Century Revolution
(1993). He offered creative reinterpretations of the writings and thought of John Milton and John Bunyan, linking each as never before to the radicalism of the English Revolution. His breadth of knowledge, his curiosity, his open-­mindedness, his love of literature, his command of chronology, and his respect for the humanity of his subjects—all of this was evident on every page of every book he wrote.
Michael Braddick’s new book,
Christopher Hill: The Life of a Radical Historian
, offers the first full and comprehensive interpretation of his subject’s life, work, and politics. Braddick admits at the outset that the reserved and private Hill “is not an easy subject for a biographer” and that his book is “more an intellectual life than a biography.” Braddick has conducted impressive research in Hill’s papers at Oxford and the thousands of pages of his published work. As a specialist in Hill’s own field, 17th-century England, Braddick brings to the project deep knowledge of the scholarship by both Hill and his critics. His account is shaped by his affiliation with the “revisionists,” led by John Morrill, who over the past 30 years have worked hard to displace Hill as the leading interpreter of the English Revolution, criticizing him for a teleological bias, determinism, anachronism, and his concept of “bourgeois revolution.” But anyone working in this area of history will have prior disagreements given the immense influence that Hill cast upon his particular field and the profession as a whole. In fact, we are hardly impartial ourselves, as Hill inspired our book
The Many-Headed Hydra
, which we dedicated to him and to his wife, Bridget Hill.
Standing at 5-foot-7, Hill had a sturdy physical presence (he’d been a rugby player in his youth) and a mischievous and ready wit that he often used in self-deprecating ways. He once quipped that he had done a “brave and creditable” job training on a light machine gun for service in World War II, adding: “A thousand pities it was on somebody else’s target.” He also had a stammer, a source of his lifelong shyness and reserve, and described himself as “mean,” by which he meant “cheap.” (His use of pencils endlessly sharpened down to an inch or less was a family joke.)
Hill’s most characteristic trait was his easy egalitarian manner. Former Oxford student Ved Mehta noted that Hill “was singular among dons…that all distinctions of degree, rank, and age were repugnant to him. He was devoid of race prejudice of any kind, and so far ahead of his time that he treated women no differently from men, without a hint of condescension.” Hill’s niece, the historian Penelope Corfield, noted that this commitment to equality, formed early in life, drove his turn toward radicalism in the 1930s.

data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种名为Group Query Attention（GQA）的技术，该技术通过共享键和值的投影来减少多头注意力机制中的内存使用。与传统的Multi-Head Attention（MHA）不同，GQA使用较少的键和值头（$N_{kv}$），并将它们共享给多个查询头（$N_h$），从而降低计算成本和内存占用。具体实现中，先将输入序列通过线性变换得到查询、键和值，然后对键和值进行分组共享，以减少缓存大小。GQA在保持模型性能的同时，显著提高了推理速度并降低了内存需求，特别适用于大型模型的部署。Multi-Query Attention（MQA）是GQA的一种极端形式，其中$N_{kv}$为1。

Attention Wasn't All We Needed
There's a lot of modern techniques that have been developed since the original
Attention Is All You Need
paper. Let's look at some of the most important ones that have been developed over the years and try to implement the basic ideas as succinctly as possible. We'll use the Pytorch framework for most of the examples. Note that most of these examples are highly simplified sketches of the core ideas, if you want the full implementation please read the original paper or the production code in frameworks like PyTorch or Jax.
Group Query Attention
Multi-head Latent Attention
Flash Attention
Ring Attention
Pre-normalization
RMSNorm
SwiGLU
Rotary Positional Embedding
Mixture of Experts
Learning Rate Warmup
Cosine Schedule
AdamW Optimizer
Multi-token Prediction
Speculative Decoding
Group Query Attention
Ok starting off in no particular order,
Grouped Query Attention
is a technique to reduce the memory usage of the KV cache during inference.  Group Query Attention is an architectural optimization for the standard multi-head attention mechanism. The core idea behind GQA is based on the observation that the computational bottleneck and memory footprint in MHA are heavily influenced by the size of the K and V projections and their corresponding caches. GQA proposes to reduce this cost by sharing a single set of K and V projections across multiple Q heads. Instead of having \(N_h\) distinct heads for Q, K, and V (as in MHA), GQA uses \(N_h\) query heads but only \(N_{kv}\) key/value heads, where \(N_{kv} < N_h\) and \(N_h\) is typically a multiple of \(N_{kv}\). These \(N_h\) query heads are divided into \(N_{kv}\) groups, with each group of \(N_h / N_{kv}\) query heads attending to the
same
key and value head. This structure significantly reduces the parameter count for
K
and
V
projection matrices and, more importantly, shrinks the size of the K/V cache needed during autoregressive decoding.
Let the input sequence representation be \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times d_{\text{model}}}\), where \(L\) is the sequence length and \(d_{\text{model}}\) is the embedding dimension. GQA first projects \(X\) into queries, keys, and values using different linear transformations: \(Q = XW_Q\), \(K = XW_K\), and \(V = XW_V\). Here, \(W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times (N_h d_k)}\), \(W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times (N_{kv} d_k)}\), and \(W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times (N_{kv} d_k)}\), where \(d_k\) is the dimension of each head (
head_dim
). These are reshaped into \(N_h\) query heads \(Q_i \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times d_k}\) (\(i=1...N_h\)) and \(N_{kv}\) key/value heads \(K_j, V_j \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times d_k}\) (\(j=1...N_{kv}\)). The key step in GQA is sharing: for the \(i\)-th query head, the corresponding key and value heads are \(K_{\lceil i / g \rceil}\) and \(V_{\lceil i / g \rceil}\), where \(g = N_h / N_{kv}\) is the group size (number of queries per KV head). The attention output for the \(i\)-th head is computed as:
$$
\text{Attention}(Q_i, K_{\lceil i / g \rceil}, V_{\lceil i / g \rceil}) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q_i K_{\lceil i / g \rceil}^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V_{\lceil i / g \rceil}
$$
In implementation, we do this by computing the \(N_{kv}\) key/value heads and then repeating or interleaving them \(g\) times to match the \(N_h\) query heads before the batched matrix multiplication for attention scores, as shown in the
repeat_interleave
step in the example code. Finally, the outputs of all \(N_h\) heads are concatenated and passed through an output projection \(W_O\).
GQA is primarily used as a technique to accelerate inference speed and reduce memory requirements without significantly compromising model performance. During autoregressive generation, the previously computed keys and values for the context sequence are cached and reused for subsequent token predictions. The size of this K/V cache is directly proportional to the number of K/V heads (\(N_{kv}\) in GQA, \(N_h\) in MHA). By reducing \(N_{kv}\), GQA drastically cuts down the memory bandwidth needed to load the K/V cache at each decoding step, which is the main performance bottleneck.
While it might slightly reduce the model's representational capacity compared to MHA (as K/V projections are shared), empirical results show that GQA achieves a favorable trade-off, maintaining most of the quality of MHA while offering substantial speedups and memory savings, making it popular for deploying large models efficiently. Multi-query attention (MQA), where \(N_{kv}=1\), is an extreme form of GQA.

44060800.article_content:
Machinist and Machine
I love coding so much. I don't mean software, I mean just writing code and
talking to the machine. Many nights I open blank emacs and just stare at the
non-blinking block cursor until something comes out. The sillier the better.
Even if it's just a few symbols, sometimes its just for (;;);. Sometimes I open
code that I consider beautiful, some Tromp diagrams, or K&R code.
Every day I am reminded how far I am from truly understanding complexity and
programmable machines.
Now most code I write is just tokens. Tens of thousands of tokens per day,
empty. I skim through them to decide if they will work or not, accept or reject
them. Again, and again... I have no empathy or emotion towards them, I feel
nothing, I have become the computer that evaluates them. From machinist to
machine. I can feel it. I can feel how it is taking me away from the path of
understanding. Every day, little by little. You must have noticed it too.
I miss it. I miss programming. People say this is what love is, when you miss
something so much, it hurts. When the pain is gone, there will be nothing, but
fire. I will fuel this fire.
I am going back, back to the wires, making my own computers, my own operating
systems, my own languages. Pointless, useless, by myself, for myself. [1] [2]
Back to become a better machinist. Listening to Man on the Silver Mountain, and
watching the block cursor at night.
By day, I will just pretend to be a machine, and evaluate the tokens, and that is OK.
PS: I am totally OK with AI upgrading my react native dependencies though :)
[1]:
Making a SUBLEQ computer
[2]:
Running: 769880310889
The path is long. The fire burns. Gilgamesh says: When there's no way out, you just follow the way in front of you.

data.title: Google's AI Mode is 'the definition of theft,' publishers say
data.author: ironyman
data.article_summary: 谷歌推出的新AI模式引发了出版商的强烈不满，被指责为“盗窃行为”，因为该模式未经允许使用出版商的内容，导致其流量和收入减少。尽管谷歌曾考虑让出版商选择退出AI模式，但最终未实施这一选项。出版商若要退出AI工具，就不得不完全退出谷歌搜索，这使其陷入两难境地。谷歌辩称其AI工具帮助引导用户访问相关网站，但出版商认为这威胁到了他们的生存，可能迫使他们转向生产廉价内容以维持生计。这一问题亟需解决，以避免互联网内容质量的进一步恶化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：谷歌垄断问题及其影响，特别是涉及Chrome、搜索与AdSense的关系、出版行业的利益受损以及知识产权（IP）在AI时代的争议。

不同观点：
• **谷歌垄断的核心来源**：
  - [jxjnskkzxxhx]：谷歌的垄断核心不在于Chrome，而在于其控制了网站流量分配和网站获利方式，即搜索和AdSense的结合。要拆分谷歌，应该从分离搜索和AdSense入手，而不是针对Chrome。
  
• **AI与就业的冲突**：
  - [rvnx]：技术进步如自动化电梯取代电梯操作员是不可避免的，创造更好技术的人无需为旧岗位消失负责。AI取代某些工作是类似的技术进步结果。

• **出版商的责任与用户体验**：
  - [j_timberlake]：尽管对出版商不公平，但出版商通过广告、弹窗等方式驱使用户离开网站，因此用户不会为他们的损失感到同情。

• **AI时代的知识产权争议**：
  - [spacebanana7]：IP法难以在LLM（大型语言模型）上执行，尤其在中国开源LLM的背景下。西方政府不会容忍对中国LLM的依赖，宁愿牺牲出版商的部分产权。
  - [constantcrying]：IP概念本身有问题，人类和AI都利用已有材料进行自我提升，而这些材料往往被严格控制，应该对所有人自由开放。

• **AI与内容分发及收益的新模式**：
  - [tippytippytango]：需要新的IP框架来激励人们在AI主导的世界中继续创作内容。
  - [jmathai]：出版商选择退出AI模式是否真的有实质性区别？考虑到谷歌控制了大部分流量分发，退出虽避免内容“被盗用”，但也失去主要的分发渠道。
  - [ivape]：LLM应该标明其内容来源，类似于新的“页面浏览量”概念，用户可以拒绝首次答案并深入搜索，类似于过去深入谷歌搜索结果页。

补充讨论：
• **对谷歌行为的批评与支持**：
  - [zb3]：谷歌创造了SEO的混乱局面，现在他们有责任结束这个问题。
  - [puppycodes]：出版行业的困境不值得过多关注，谷歌在更大层面上有更严重的问题，如知识产权的“疯狂”现状。
  - [josefritzishere]：谷歌正在滥用其垄断地位，需要被拆分。

争议焦点：谷歌垄断的核心是否在于Chrome，还是在于其控制流量和收益分配的方式；出版商是否应为用户流失负责；在AI和LLM时代，如何保护和调整知识产权以适应新的技术环境。

44075346.article_content:
Google Search
Google AI Mode
Google’s AI Mode is ‘the definition of theft,’ publishers say, opt-out was considered
Ben Schoon
| May 22 2025 - 9:35 am PT
13 Comments
The AI takeover of Search is in full swing, especially as
Google’s new AI Mode is going live for all US users
. But for publishers, this continues the existential crisis around how Google Search is changing, with a new statement calling AI Mode “the definition of theft” while legal documents reveal that Google did consider opt out controls that ultimately weren’t implemented.
In a
statement
earlier this week, the News/Media Alliance slammed Google for “further depriving publishers of original content both traffic and revenue.” The full statement reads:
Links were the last redeeming quality of search that gave publishers traffic and revenue. Now Google just takes content by force and uses it with no return, the definition of theft. The DOJ remedies must address this to prevent continued domination of the internet by one company.
This comes right as new
documents
revealed that Google had weighed out several options regarding allowing publishers to opt out of “SGE” – what ultimately became AI Overviews – but decided against these options (via
Bloomberg
).
Google’s options range from making no changes whatsoever to publisher controls, to explicit separation between Google’s AI tools and the rest of Search, something the company called a “hard red line,” implying that option was never being considered.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
As it stands today, publishers are unable to opt out of Google’s AI tools without effectively opting out of Search as a whole. Google considers this “Option 2,” where publishers can limit how often their content is used for AI results by opting out of traditional “snippets,” which don’t appear as often with the rise of AI Overviews anyway.
The documents distinctly show that Google chose not to announce any of this publicly and avoid saying that making changes opts publishers out of seeing their work used for training data.
Google, speaking to
Bloomberg
regarding these documents, said:
Publishers have always controlled how their content is made available to Google as AI models have been built into Search for many years, helping surface relevant sites and driving traffic to them. This document is an early-stage list of options in an evolving space and doesn’t reflect feasibility or actual decisions.
9to5Google’s Take
It’s not hard to see why Google went the route that it did here. Giving publishers the ability to opt out of AI products while still benefiting from Search would ultimately make Google’s flashy new tools useless if enough sites made the switch. It was very much a move in the interest of building a better product.
Does that change anything regarding how Google’s AI products in Search cause potential harm to the publishing industry?
Nope.
Google’s tools continue to serve the company and its users (mostly) well, but as they continue to bleed publishers dry, those publishers are on the
verge of vanishing
or, arguably worse, turning to
cheap and poorly produced content
just to get enough views to survive. This is a problem Google needs to address, as it’s making the internet as a whole worse for everyone.

data.title: Avoiding becoming the lone dependency peg with load-bearing anime
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了作者在开发Web AI防火墙工具Anubis时，为何在挑战屏幕上默认显示一个动漫角色Aoi。这个角色作为一种“购物车测试”，目的是确保项目可持续，并避免作者独自承担过多的无偿工作。用户可以选择替换这些艺术资产，但作者更希望他们通过购买商业版本来支持项目。动漫图像的存在引发了一些争议，但也起到了病毒式营销的效果。作者提到正在开发无JavaScript的解决方案，并考虑使用WebAssembly来防止 scrapers。作者还申请了NLNet资助，并获得了风投兴趣，希望通过这些途径支持项目的持续发展。最后，作者呼吁用户通过GitHub Sponsors进行捐助以支持项目。
